数学预备知识
Mathematical Prerequisites

prereqs · Page 1

Although CS103 is primarily a math class, this course does not require any higher math as a prerequisite. The most advanced level of mathematics you'll need for this course is high school algebra. Anything beyond that – trigonometry, complex numbers, calculus, limits, and (especially) graphing functions on a coordinate axis – isn't necessary for the course and won't come up at all over the course of the quarter.

This page outlines the particular skills and concepts we'll assume you have seen on entry to this class. As you'll find out quickly, the sort of math that we'll be doing looks very little like the math that you probably did in high school, so even if you are a bit shaky on these concepts, you should be fine in this class.

CS103 虽然是数学课, 但不需要高等数学作基础, 最多用到高中代数. 三角、复数、微积分、极限、在坐标系里画函数图像都用不到. 这份指南列出课程默认学生已经会的六项技能. 课程里的数学和高中数学很不一样 (重证明而不是计算), 所以这些不太熟也没关系.

多项式乘法与等式变形
Skill 1: Multiplying Polynomials · Skill 2: Manipulating Equalities

prereqs · Page 1–2

Early on this course (and, surprisingly, not much beyond then), we'll assume that you know how to multiply two polynomials together. For example, in one of our early proofs, we're going to arrive at the equation n2=(2k)2 and will simplify the right-hand side to get that n2=4k2. Similarly, on Friday, we'll end up with the equation n2=(2k+1)2 and will simplify the right-hand side to conclude that n2=4k2+4k+1.

Oddly enough, we won't be factoring many – if any – polynomials over the quarter. … we certainly won't be dividing polynomials, so don't lose any sleep over that.

This skill from high school algebra is the one we'll get the most mileage out of in this class. … Imagine that you know that 2x+3=5 and you want to solve for x. To do so, you could subtract three from both sides to get 2x=2 and then divide both sides by two to get that x=1.

Sometimes, in CS103, we'll write out a long chain of equalities to show that two numbers or quantities happen to be equal to one another. For example, we might show that (2n+1)2−(2n)2=4n+1 by writing out something like this:

(2n+1)2−(2n)2​=4n2+4n+1−4n2=(4n2−4n2)+4n+1=4n+1.​

Here, the top line performs one simplification, and each line after that is a simplification from the previous line. The final result is that the left-hand side of the first equality ends up being equal to the right-hand side of the last equality.

技能 1: 会展开多项式乘积. 课上最早的证明 (偶数的平方是偶数、奇数的平方是奇数) 就要把 (2k)2 展开成 4k2, 把 (2k+1)2 展开成 4k2+4k+1. 因式分解几乎用不到, 多项式除法完全用不到.

技能 2: 会变形等式, 这是全课用得最多的高中技能. 一是两边同做一个运算 (两边减 3、两边除以 2); 二是写等式链: 每一行只比上一行多化简一步, 最后第一行的左边就等于最后一行的右边. 证明里写等式链时, 每一步都应该能一眼看出为什么成立.

指数与根
Skill 3: Working with Exponents and Roots

prereqs · Page 2

There are a few properties of exponents that we'll be using over the course of this class … The first is what happens if you multiply together two powers of some number x: xa⋅xb=xa+b.

This property of exponents is fundamental – exponents are often used precisely because they turn multiplication into addition. … One special case of this result that comes up a few times in CS103 is this one: xn+1=x⋅xn. For example, 2n+1=2⋅2n=2n+2n. We'll use this specific fact when we talk about induction around the halfway point of the quarter.

Another property is what happens if you raise one number to a power, then raise that to the power of another number. Specifically: (xa)b=xab=(xb)a.

The last key property we'll need is the connection between roots and exponents. … whatever number x1/2 is, it has the property that, when you multiply it by itself, you get x. We have another name for that number – it's the square root of x! So this means that x1/2=x​, and, more generally, that x1/a=ax​.

技能 3: 三条指数法则. ① xa⋅xb=xa+b, 指数把乘法变成加法; 特例 xn+1=x⋅xn, 例如 2n+1=2n+2n, 归纳法证明 20+⋯+2n=2n+1−1 时就用它 (见 CS103 12). ② (xa)b=xab, 当 a、b 是正整数时可以由 ① 推出: xa 自乘 b 次, 指数相加 b 次. ③ 分数指数就是根: x1/2 自乘得到 x, 所以它就是 x​.

数的种类与封闭性
Skill 4: Categorizing Types of Numbers · Skill 5: Using Closure Properties

prereqs · Page 2–3

The numbers we'll use the most extensively throughout the quarter – and which seem to get used more than any other type in all of computer science – are the natural numbers. These are the numbers 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, …, etc. They're the whole numbers (no fractions or decimals allowed) starting at 0 and continuing on toward infinity. However, we don't consider ∞ to be a natural number.

The next class of numbers we'll be using are the integers. They're basically things you can store in an int: …, −3, −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, 3, …, etc., except that there's no limit to how large or small the numbers can be. … The last “fundamental” class of numbers we'll deal with are the real numbers. These are all the numbers that exist on the number line: 0, 1, ½, π, −3, −137⁄42, −e², etc.

… “the natural numbers are closed under addition.” In other words, if you start with two natural numbers and add them together, you're guaranteed to get back a natural number. However, if you subtract two natural numbers, you are not guaranteed to get back a natural number.

+−×÷
Natural NumbersYesYes
IntegersYesYesYes
Real NumbersYesYesYesYes

The closure properties of the natural numbers, integers, and real numbers are usually considered so fundamental that they're not really talked about in proofs even though they often play a major role in them.

技能 4: 分清三类数. natural numbers 自然数 N = {0, 1, 2, …}, CS103 里 0 是自然数, ∞ 不是. integers 整数 Z 包括负数. real numbers 实数 R 是数轴上所有的数. 自然数 ⊂ 整数 ⊂ 实数. 复数本课不用.

技能 5: closure property 封闭性. 「自然数对加法封闭」指两个自然数相加一定还是自然数. 表格汇总: 自然数对加、乘封闭, 对减 (3 − 5 = −2)、除 (137 ÷ 2) 不封闭; 整数多了减法; 实数四则运算都封闭 (除数不为 0). 证明里常常默默用到这些性质, 比如「k 是整数, 所以 2k² + 2k 也是整数」. 后面讲正则语言时还会说「正则语言对克林星号封闭」, 是同一个概念的推广.

不等式与整数
Skill 6: Manipulating Inequalities

prereqs · Page 4

There's one particular set of rules for inequalities that is sometimes covered in high-school algebra and sometimes skipped, and that's what happens when you work with inequalities involving integers. For example, consider the inequality 2<x<3. … If x is allowed to be a real number, then there are lots of values of x that satisfy this inequality, such as 2.5, 2.1, or 2.71828. However, if x is an integer or a natural number, then there are no choices of x that make this true, since there aren't any integers between 2 and 3.

… Let's imagine that n is a natural number. Then the inequality 2<n is exactly the same as the inequality 3≤n. … More generally, let's imagine that m and n are integers or natural numbers. In that case, the inequality m<n is exactly the same as the inequality m+1≤n.

技能 6: 整数上的不等式. 2 和 3 之间没有整数, 所以对整数 n, 2<n 等价于 3≤n; 一般地, 整数 m、n 满足 m<n 当且仅当 m+1≤n. 对实数这不成立 (2.5 满足前者不满足后者). 这条在鸽巢原理和归纳法的证明里会用到, 例如「n ≥ 1 的整数」与「n > 0 的整数」可以互换.

结尾: 讲师教过约 4000 名学生, 从没遇到数学准备不够上不了这门课的人.

∈ 与 ⊆ 指南
Guide to ∈ and ⊆

elements_and_subsets · Page 1

(这份是一个 176 页动画指南的截图, 只能看到前三页.)

Guide to ∈ and ⊆

Hi everybody!

In our first lecture on sets and set theory, we introduced a bunch of new symbols and terminology.

这份指南讲第一讲引入的两个最容易混的符号: ∈ (属于) 和 ⊆ (子集). 截图只有开头几页.

两者的区别 (CS103 00 的内容, 这里集中复习): x∈S 说 x 是 S 的一个元素; A⊆S 说 A 是一个集合, 它的每个元素都在 S 里. 判断方法:

  • x∈S: 把 S 的元素一个个列出来, 看 x 是不是其中之一 (整体作为一个元素).
  • A⊆S: A 必须是集合; 把 A 的花括号拆开, 看里面每个元素是不是都在 S 的列表里.

例子: 设 S={1,2,{3}}. 则 1∈S, {1}⊆S, {3}∈S (它是 S 的一个元素), 但 {3}⊆S (3 不是 S 的元素), 而 {{3}}⊆S. 空集 ∅ 是任何集合的子集 (空真), 但 ∅∈S 只在 S 真的把空集列为元素时成立. 与幂集的联系: A⊆S 当且仅当 A∈℘(S).

证明指南
Guide to Proofs

guide_to_proofs · Page 1

Writing mathematical proofs is a skill that combines both creative problem-solving and standardized, formal writing. When you're first learning to write proofs, this can seem like a lot to take in. However, there are certain patterns in proof writing that, once internalized, make the whole endeavor a lot easier. This page covers those patterns and is designed to help you take your first steps into Theoryland.

写证明既要有创造性的解题, 又要遵守标准化的写作格式. 这份指南讲的是格式部分: 每种命题都有固定的开头和结尾, 掌握后即使还不知道为什么成立, 也能先把证明的框架搭起来. 它是 CS103 01 和 02 的配套材料.

直接证明: 蕴涵式
Direct Proofs: Implications

guide_to_proofs · Page 1–2

As a reminder, an implication is a statement of the form If P is true, then Q is true. … the antecedent of this implication is the statement “P is true,” and the consequent of this implication is the statement “Q is true.”

… all these proofs more or less follow the same basic structure. Specifically, you assume the antecedent is true, and then you prove the consequent is true. … For example, let's take the following (nonsense) implication: If x is a pizkwat, then x is a squigglebah.

Proof: Assume that x is a pizkwat. We need to show that x is a squigglebah. […]

We call the first part of this proof (“Assume that x is a pizkwat”) the assume step and the second part of this proof (“We need to show that x is a squigglebah”) the want-to-show.

Proof: Assume that x is a pizkwat. We need to show that x is a squigglebah.
(the actual logic of the proof goes here)
This means that x is a squigglebah, which is what we needed to show. ■

To summarize, to prove an implication, do the following:

  1. Write your assume step. This is where you assume the antecedent is true.
  2. Write your want-to-show step. This is where you say that you will show the consequent is true.
  3. Write the actual reasoning. Manipulate what you're given in your assume step until you arrive at the claim you made in your want-to-show step. This is the creative part of the proof.
  4. Return to your want-to-show. Indicate to the reader that you ended up where you said you were going to end up, and end the proof with a nice ■ symbol.

蕴涵式 "If P, then Q": P 叫 antecedent 前件, Q 叫 consequent 后件. 直接证明的格式永远是: 假设前件成立, 证明后件成立. 所以哪怕是 pizkwat、squigglebah 这种编造的词, 也能写出第一句 "假设 x 是 pizkwat, 我们要证 x 是 squigglebah".

四步: ① assume step 假设步, 写出假设; ② want-to-show 目标句, 写出要证什么; ③ 中间推理 (唯一需要创造力的部分); ④ 回到目标句: "这说明 x 是 squigglebah, 正是要证的", 画 ■. 措辞可以换 (Suppose / Let …, We will prove …), 但必须让读者看清你假设了什么、要证什么.

guide_to_proofs · Page 2

Exercises — try applying this rule to start off proofs of the following statements. … just write the first sentence or two, along with the last sentence.

  1. If the Riemann Hypothesis is true, then P = NP. (These are real mathematical terms. We have no reason to believe that they're related.)
  2. If every peganil number is also a retract, then each requint is wobbly. (These are nonsense terms. I made them up because they sound funny.)
  3. If UTM​ is a TM that halts on a string w, then UTM​ accepts ⟨M,w⟩. (You'll know what this means later in the quarter!)

练习: 只写开头和结尾. 例如 (i): "Proof: Assume the Riemann Hypothesis is true. We need to show that P = NP. … Thus P = NP, as required. ■" (ii) 同理: 假设每个 peganil 数都是 retract, 要证每个 requint 都是 wobbly. (iii) 假设 UTM​ 在 w 上停机, 要证它接受 ⟨M,w⟩. 这三句话本身都不需要懂这些术语.

直接证明: 全称命题
Direct Proofs: Universally-Quantified Statements

guide_to_proofs · Page 2–4

A universally-quantified statement is a statement that makes a claim about all objects of some type. … each universally-quantified statement will consist of two parts:

  • A placeholder variable representing an object of some type.
  • A claim about that placeholder variable that is true regardless of the choice made.

The general pattern for proving a universally-quantified statement with a direct proof is as follows:

  1. Instruct the reader to pick an arbitrary object of the appropriate type and give it a name.
  2. Prove the object the reader has picked necessarily has the required property.

Theorem: Every natural number n can be written as the sum of four perfect squares.
Proof: Pick a natural number n. We want to show that n can be written as the sum of four perfect squares. […]

… First, it indicates that you, the person writing the proof, are not actually selecting any specific natural number to reason about. Instead, you're telling the person reading your proof that they have full control here. … Second, it gives a concrete meaning to the variable name n. In the statement of the theorem, the variable n doesn't actually refer to anything. It's a placeholder for “whatever number you want it to be.”

As a note, “pick a natural number n” is not the only way to write this out. … Consider a natural number n. · Let n∈N be an arbitrary natural number. · Fix some n∈N. (Note: “fix” here means “pin down,” not “repair.”) · Choose some n∈N.

universally-quantified statement 全称命题: 对某类的所有对象断言某性质. 它由占位变量和关于它的断言组成; 没写变量的 ("每个自然数都能写成四个平方数之和") 可以自己补一个 n.

证法: 让读者任选一个该类对象并命名, 然后证明它一定有所需性质. "Pick a natural number n" 有两层意思: ① 不是作者挑了某个特定的数, 而是读者想选什么都行, 证明对任何选择都成立; ② 给 n 一个确定的含义, 之后各句话里的 n 都指同一个数. 定理陈述里的 n 只是占位符, 不指任何东西.

结构同样是四步: 让读者任选并命名 → 目标句 → 推理 → 回到目标句画 ■. 易错: "Fix some n" 的 fix 是「固定下来」, 不是「修理」.

guide_to_proofs · Page 4

Exercises — sketch out what the shape of the proof might look like.

  1. For every NFA N, there is a DFA D where L(N)=L(D). (You'll learn what this means later this quarter!)
  2. For every integer n, there are integers r and s where r2−s2=4n. (Great exercise!)
  3. Every Siegel field has a cofinal attractor. (These are mathy-sounding terms I made up. They aren't real things.)

(i) "Pick an arbitrary NFA N. We will show that there is a DFA D where ℒ(N) = ℒ(D). …" (这正是子集构造要做的, 见 CS103 15). (iii) 先补变量: "Let F be an arbitrary Siegel field. We need to show that F has a cofinal attractor." (ii) 外层全称、内层存在, 下一节讲.

拆开复合命题
Unpacking Compound Statements

guide_to_proofs · Page 4–5

It's common to see statements that combine together a universally-quantified statement and an implication. For example: For any integer n, if n is even, then n² is even.

Proof: Pick an integer n. We will show that if n is even, then n² is even. To do so, assume n is even. We need to show that n² is even.
( the actual logic of the proof goes here )
Thus n² is even, as required. ■

This pattern – writing out an initial want-to-show and then expanding that out into another want-to-show – is something we call unpacking. … In the specific case of a universally-quantified implication (“for any x, if P(x) is true, then Q(x) is true”), it's often a bit easier to combine the introduction of the variable from the quantified bit and the assumption from the antecedent.

Proof: Pick an even integer n. We will show that n² is even. … Thus n² is even, as required. ■

Exercises: i. For all languages L, if L is regular, then L is regular. ii. For any rectible integer x, if x is Egan-prime, then G[x, 2] is unobserved. iii. For any integers x, y, and z, if x2+y2=z2, then (x+1)2+(y+1)2=(z+1)2.

"对任意整数 n, 若 n 是偶数则 n² 是偶数" 外层是全称, 里面是蕴涵. 逐层拆开 (unpacking): 先按全称的格式选 n, 目标变成一个蕴涵; 再按蕴涵的格式假设 n 是偶数, 目标变成 "n² 是偶数". 常见的简写是把两步合并: "Pick an even integer n", 效果相同, 因为 n 都是 ① 整数 ② 读者任选 ③ 偶数.

练习 (i): "Let L be a regular language. We will show that L is regular." (iii): "Pick integers x, y, z where x2+y2=z2. We need to show that (x+1)2+(y+1)2=(z+1)2." 这题其实很容易: 两边相减并用 x2+y2=z2, 左边 − 右边 = 2(x + y − z) + 1, 是奇数, 不可能为 0.

直接证明: 存在命题
Direct Proofs: Existentially-Quantified Statements

guide_to_proofs · Page 6–7

An existentially-quantified statement is one that states that there is at least one object with some property. … For example: There is a positive integer x equal to the sum of all smaller positive integers. There is a one-state NFA N that does not accept all strings.

… the general pattern for proving an existentially-quantified statement with a direct proof is to simply find what that object is and then prove it indeed has the needed properties.

Theorem: There is a swipestone x such that x is edurable. Proof: Pick x = ___. We need to show that x is a swipestone and x is edurable. ( the actual proof that x has those properties ) Thus x is an edurable swipestone, as required. ■

The key difference between this style of proof and a proof of a universally-quantified statement is that, in this case, we are specifically telling the reader what object we're picking.

… For any integer n, there are integers r and s where r2−s2=4n.

Proof: Pick some integer n. We want to show that there are integers r and s where r2−s2=4n. Pick r = ___ and s = ___. We then see that ( some proof that r2−s2=4n ) Thus r2−s2=4n, as required. ■

A great exercise: what choices of r and s should you make here?

existentially-quantified statement 存在命题: 至少有一个对象具有某性质. 证法是直接给出那个对象, 再验证它满足要求. 和全称命题的关键区别: 这里是作者指定对象, 不能让读者随便挑, 因为大多数选择不满足.

两个例子: 等于所有更小正整数之和的正整数, 取 x = 3 (= 1 + 2); 不接受所有串的单状态 NFA, 取唯一状态不是接受状态的 NFA.

全称套存在: 先让读者任选 n, 再由作者根据 n 构造 r 和 s. 留下的练习答案: 取 r = n + 1, s = n − 1, 则 (n+1)2−(n−1)2=4n. 注意 r、s 可以依赖 n, 因为 n 先选定.

双条件命题
Direct Proofs: Biconditionals

guide_to_proofs · Page 7

A biconditional is a statement of the form P is true if and only if Q is true. … For example: If n is an integer, then n is even if and only if n² is even. There is a DFA D for a language L if and only if there is an NFA N for language L.

… a biconditional consists of two separate implications. … the general strategy for proving a biconditional is to write out two separate proofs, one for each of the two implications.

Proof: Pick an arbitrary x. We will prove both directions of implication.
First, we will prove that if x is spirocontractive, then x is chiroshrinking. (Insert a proof of that implication here. You can do this directly by then assuming the antecedent and proving the consequent, or using the contrapositive, or using a proof by contradiction, whichever floats your boat.)
Next, we will prove that if x is chiroshrinking, then x is spirocontractive. (…) ■

biconditional 双条件 "P 当且仅当 Q" 就是两个蕴涵: P → Q 和 Q → P. 证明就是两个独立的证明粘在一起, 先宣布 "两个方向都要证", 然后各自用任何方法 (直接、逆否、反证) 证明. 例: "n 是偶数 ⟺ n² 是偶数", 一个方向直接证, 另一个方向用逆否 (见 CS103 02).

逆否证明与反证法
Proof by Contrapositive · Proof by Contradiction

guide_to_proofs · Page 8

In a proof by contrapositive, instead of proving the original implication, you'll prove a different implication. Specifically, instead of proving the statement If P is true, then Q is true, you'll prove the statement If Q is false, then P is false.

  1. Start off by announcing that you're going to prove the contrapositive of the statement you wish to prove. … Don't skip this step! … First, it communicates to the reader what they should expect in the proof … Second, it forces you to write out the contrapositive of the statement that you're trying to prove, reducing the likelihood that you accidentally take the contrapositive incorrectly.
  2. Using any proof technique you'd like, prove the contrapositive of the statement.

Proof: We will prove that if x is an omnesiac, then x is amniscient. To do so, we will instead prove the contrapositive, that if x is not amniscient, then x is not an amnesiac.
Pick any x that is not amniscient. We want to show that x is not an omnesiac. ( the actual logic goes here ) So x is not an omnesiac, as required. ■

逆否证明: 不证 "P → Q", 改证等价的 "非 Q → 非 P". 第一步一定要宣布用逆否, 并写出逆否命题: 让读者知道接下来证的是什么, 也逼自己把逆否写对. "All omnesiacs are amniscient" 看起来不是蕴涵, 但可以改写成 "对所有 x, 若 x 是 omnesiac 则 x 是 amniscient", 于是也能用逆否.

原文笔误: 示范证明里的逆否命题写成 "then x is not an amnesiac", 应为 "not an omnesiac" (与前后两句一致). 编造的词拼错了一个, 不影响结构.

guide_to_proofs · Page 9

In a proof by contradiction, to prove that some statement P is true, you instead assume that P is false, then proceed to derive an impossible statement (a contradiction).

  1. Start off by saying that you're going to write a proof by contradiction. For example, you could write “Assume for the sake of contradiction that …” … Then, explicitly write out the negation of the statement you're trying to prove.
  2. Starting with your assumption from part (1), proceed to conclude something impossible, such as that 1 = 0, that a number is both even and odd, that something is an element of the empty set, that ∣S∣=∣℘(S)∣, etc.
  3. State that you've reached a contradiction and, if it's not obvious, explain why it's a logical contradiction.
  4. Conclude the proof. I commonly say something to the effect of “We have reached a contradiction, so our assumption must have been wrong, so […].”
If you want to prove this by contradiction...... assume this.
All P's are Q'sSome P is not a Q
No P's are Q'sSome P is a Q
Some P's are Q'sAll P's are not Q's
Some P is not a QAll P's are Q's
If P is true, then Q is trueP is true and Q is false
P is true and Q is trueP is false, or Q is false, or both are false
P is true, Q is true, or both are trueP is false and Q is false

反证法四步: ① 宣布用反证, 并明确写出要证命题的否定; ② 从该假设推出不可能的结论 (1 = 0、一个数既奇又偶、某物属于空集、∣S∣=∣℘(S)∣ 与康托尔定理矛盾); ③ 指出这是矛盾, 不明显时解释为什么; ④ 收尾: 假设错了, 所以原命题成立.

表格是常用命题的否定: "所有 P 都是 Q" 的否定是 "有某个 P 不是 Q"; "若 P 则 Q" 的否定是 "P 真且 Q 假" (不是另一个蕴涵); "P 且 Q" 的否定是 "P 假或 Q 假"; "P 或 Q" 的否定是 "P 假且 Q 假" (德摩根律). 系统方法见下面的 FOL 检查清单和 CS103 05.

分情况证明
Proof by Cases

guide_to_proofs · Page 9–10

Theorem: If n is an integer, then n2≡2​n. (The notation ≡2​ is defined on Problem Set One.)

Proof: Pick some integer n. We need to show that n2≡2​n. To see this, we consider two cases:

Case 1: n is even. This means that there is an integer k where n = 2k. We then see that n2=2kn=2k+2kn−2k=n+2(kn−k). This means there is an integer m, namely, kn − k, such that n2=n+2m. Thus n2≡2​n.

Case 2: n is odd. Then there's an integer k where n = 2k + 1, which means that n2=(2k+1)2=4k2+4k+1=2k+1+4k2+2k=n+2(2k2+k). This means there is an integer m (namely, 2k² + k) such that n2=n+2m. Thus n2≡2​n.

In each case, we see that n2≡2​n, as required. ■

  • We announce that we are splitting into cases, which helps the reader better see where the proof is going.
  • Each case begins with a description of what that case is …
  • After splitting into cases, we summarize what we proved true in all cases …
  • Each case is considered a logically separate part of the proof from each other case, so we are allowed to reuse variable names across cases, just as we would reuse local variable names across different functions or for loops.

… Notice that we do not need to justify why our cases cover all possibilities. Usually, that's clear from context. … it's perfectly acceptable for a proof by cases to have cases that can overlap.

分情况不是独立的证明方式, 可以嵌在任何证明里: 把所有可能分成几类, 每一类里结论都成立. 例子证明 n2≡2​n (n² 与 n 奇偶相同, 即 n² − n 是偶数), 按 n 偶、n 奇分两种情况, 每种都把 n² 写成 n + 2m.

写法要点: 宣布要分情况; 每个情况开头写清这一情况的额外假设; 最后总结 "每种情况下都成立"; 不同情况是独立的作用域, 变量名 (k、m) 可以重复用, 就像不同函数里的局部变量. 情况覆盖全部可能通常不必证明 (偶/奇显然覆盖), 情况之间可以重叠 (已知 "P 或 Q" 时分 P 真、Q 真两种, 不必单列两者都真).

练习
Exercises

guide_to_proofs · Page 10–12
  1. "If my friend brings me ice cream, then I will be happy." What is the antecedent of this implication? What is the consequent?
  2. "Your car will be towed if you park here." … What it its antecedent? What is its consequent?
  3. Theorem: For all natural numbers m and n, if m is odd and n is odd, then m² + n² is odd. Which … is a better way to begin the proof? 1. "Let m and n be odd natural numbers. We need to prove that m² + n² is odd." 2. "Pick m = 3 and n = 5. We will prove that m² + n² is odd."
  4. Theorem: There exist odd natural numbers m and n where m² + n² = 34. Which … is a better way to begin the proof? (same two options, with “= 34”)
  5. Prove for all integers m and n that if m and n are odd, then mn is odd.
  6. Prove for all integers n that if n is even, then there are odd integers r and s where n = r + s.
  7. What is the negation of the following statement? "There is a natural number n where n(n + 1) is a perfect square."
  8. What is the negation of the following statement? "If someone is happy, then everyone is happy?"
  9. What is the contrapositive of the following statement? "If mn is even, then m is even or n is even."
  10. What is the contrapositive of the following statement? "If someone is happy, then everyone is happy."
  11. A natural number n is called a triangular number if there is a natural number k where n=2k(k+1)​. … Prove the following using a proof by contrapositive: for all natural numbers n, if 9n + 1 is not a triangular number, then neither is n.
  12. A real number x is called a whimsical number when there exist natural numbers a and b such that x=a+b137​. Prove, using a proof by contrapositive, that for any real numbers a and b, if ab is not whimsical, then at least one of a and b is not whimsical.
  13. You have twenty red balls and three boxes. You distribute those balls into the boxes. Prove by contradiction that some box has an even number of balls in it.

原文的答案折叠在网页里, PDF 中只有 "Solution" 字样. 以下是答案要点:

  1. 前件 "朋友给我带冰淇淋", 后件 "我会开心".
  2. 前件 "你把车停在这里", 后件 "车会被拖走". "Q if P" 的前件是 if 后面的部分.
  3. 选 1. 全称命题要让读者任选; 选 3 和 5 只证了一个特例.
  4. 选 2. 存在命题要由作者给出具体对象: 9 + 25 = 34.
  5. 设 m = 2a + 1, n = 2b + 1, 则 mn = 4ab + 2a + 2b + 1 = 2(2ab + a + b) + 1, 是奇数.
  6. 设 n 是偶数, 取 r = n − 1, s = 1, 两者都是奇数且 r + s = n.
  7. "对每个自然数 n, n(n + 1) 都不是完全平方数."
  8. "有人开心, 并且有人不开心." (蕴涵的否定是 "前件真且后件假".)
  9. "若 m 和 n 都是奇数, 则 mn 是奇数." (后件 "m 偶或 n 偶" 的否定用德摩根律.)
  10. "若有人不开心, 则所有人都不开心", 即 "若有人不开心, 则没有人开心".
  11. 证逆否: 若 n 是三角数, 则 9n + 1 也是. 设 n = k(k + 1)/2, 则 9n + 1 = (9k² + 9k + 2)/2 = (3k + 1)(3k + 2)/2, 取 j = 3k + 1 即得 9n + 1 = j(j + 1)/2.
  12. 证逆否: 若 a、b 都是 whimsical, 则 ab 也是. 设 a=p+q137​, b=r+s137​, 则 ab=(pr+137qs)+(ps+qr)137​, 两个系数都是自然数 (自然数对加法、乘法封闭).
  13. 反设每个盒子里的球数都是奇数, 三个奇数之和是奇数, 但总数 20 是偶数, 矛盾.

证明写作检查清单
Proofwriting Checklist

proofwriting_checklist · Page 1

The conventions used in mathematical proofs can generally be broken down into two areas. The first are rules on structure and writing style, which give rise to the charactistic language used in proofs. The second are rules that may initially appear stylistic, but which hit at deeper aspects of mathematical reasoning.

We have distilled many aspects of mathematical proofwriting into eight specific items that we will look for when reading (and grading) your proofs. They are as follows:

  • Clearly articulate your assumptions and “want-to-shows.”
  • Make each sentence “load-bearing.”
  • Scope and properly introduce variables.
  • Make specific claims about specific variables.
  • Don't repeat definitions; use them instead.
  • Write in complete sentences and paragraphs.
  • Avoid quantifiers and propositional connectives.
  • Avoid the “contradiction sandwich.”

We will apply this checklist to the proofs that you submit. We recommend you work through this checklist on every proof that you write.

证明的写作规范分两类: 一类是结构和文风; 另一类看似是文风, 其实关系到推理本身, 遵守它们能自动避免一整类数学错误. 课程把规范浓缩成 8 条, 批改作业时逐条检查: ① 写清假设和目标; ② 每句话都要「承重」; ③ 变量要有作用域、正确引入; ④ 对具体变量作具体断言; ⑤ 不复述定义, 而是使用定义; ⑥ 写完整的句子和段落; ⑦ 不用量词和命题联结词符号; ⑧ 避免「反证三明治」.

原文中 "charactistic" 是 "characteristic" 的拼写错误.

写清假设和目标
Clearly Articulate Your Assumptions and “Want-to-Shows.”

proofwriting_checklist · Page 1–3
  1. Introduce a set of starting assumptions, often introducing some variables in the process.
  2. Articulate the overall goal of the proof.
  3. Give some line of reasoning that reaches the goal.
  4. State you've reached the goal and end the proof.

Direct Proofs — Theorem: If m is odd and n is even, then mn is even. Proof: Pick any odd integer m and even integer n. We will show that mn is even. (… logic goes here …) This means that mn is even, as required. ■

Proof by Contrapositive — Proof: We will prove the contrapositive, namely, that if m is odd and n is odd, then mn is odd. So choose any odd integers m and n. We need to prove that mn is odd. […] This means that mn is odd, as required. ■

Proof by Contradiction — A proof by contradiction is different from the other proofwriting styles in that it always includes an assumption, but never includes a want-to-show. It is implicit in a proof by contradiction that the want-to-show is "a contradiction," so it's left out of the proof. … the conclusion of the proof explains what the contradiction shows, which is often the theorem itself.

Existential Statements — … you might want to prove that 56 is the sum of four cubes, or that 137 is the sum of two squares. In those cases, you will typically not have anything to assume … it's customary to not include an assume or want-to-show statement.

证明的一般结构: 引入假设 (常同时引入变量) → 说明目标 → 推理 → 宣布到达目标. 四种情形:

  • 直接证明: 开头写假设和目标, 结尾一定要回到目标 (目标说证 mn 是偶数, 最后一句就是 "mn 是偶数").
  • 逆否证明: 假设和目标按逆否命题写, 结尾回到逆否命题的目标.
  • 反证法: 只有假设, 没有目标句, 因为目标默认就是「推出矛盾」; 结尾说明矛盾意味着什么 (通常就是定理本身).
  • 单纯的存在命题 (56 是四个立方数之和、137 是两个平方数之和): 没什么可假设, 目标就是定理本身, 所以两样都不写, 直接给出对象并验证.
proofwriting_checklist · Page 3–4

Exercises (each: Does the following proof adhere to the style expectation outlined in this section? If not, rewrite it so that it does.)

  1. For all integers m and n, if m is even and n is even, then m + n is even. Proof: Since m is even and n is even, we know there are integers r and s where m = 2r and n = 2s. …
  2. For all integers n, if n is even, then there exist even integers r and s where r + s = n². Proof: Let n be an even integer. Since n is even, as proved in lecture we know that n² is even. Now let r = n² and s = 0. …
  3. For all integers n, if n is a multiple of three, then n² is a multiple of three. Proof: Choose any n that is a multiple of three. We need to show that n² is a multiple of three. … Therefore, for all integers n, if n is a multiple of three, then so is n². ■
  4. For all integers m and n, if m + n is odd, then so is m − n. Proof: We will prove the contrapositive, namely, that if m − n is even, then m + n is even as well. Since m − n is even, there is an integer k where m − n = 2k. This means that m + n = m − n + 2n = 2k + 2n = 2(k + n), so there is an integer s (namely, m + n) such that m + n = 2s, so m + n is even. ■
  5. For all integers m and n, if mn + 1 is even, then m is odd or n is odd. Proof: Assume for the sake of contradiction that there are integers m and n where mn + 1 is even but m is even and n is even. We will show that this results in a contradiction. …
  6. There is a natural number n where n² + 56 = 60. Proof: Pick n = 2. We then see that n² + 56 = 2² + 56 = 60, as required. ■

答案要点 (原文的答案折叠在网页中):

  1. 不符合: m、n 没有被引入 (读者没被要求选它们), 也没有目标句. 开头应改成 "Pick any even integers m and n. We will show that m + n is even."
  2. 不符合: 有假设但没有目标句. 在第一句后补 "We need to show that there are even integers r and s where r + s = n²."
  3. 符合. 最后一句重述整个定理不算错, 但写成 "Thus n² is a multiple of three, as required." 更直接.
  4. 不符合: 宣布逆否之后没有假设句和目标句 (应补 "Pick integers m and n where m − n is even. We need to show m + n is even."). 另外它的推导本身有错: s 应取 k + n, 不是 m + n.
  5. 不符合: 反证法不写目标句, "We will show that this results in a contradiction." 应删掉.
  6. 符合: 单纯的存在命题不需要假设和目标句.

每句话都要承重
Make Each Sentence Load-Bearing

proofwriting_checklist · Page 4–5

As a general rule, every statement in a proof should do one of the following things:

  • Set up a goal. … In larger proofs, you might find yourself needing to prove an auxiliary result that you'll use to build up to the larger result, and when you do that, you'll similarly want to set up what it is that you're trying to prove.
  • Introduce a new variable. … “let x be an arbitrary bananafish,” … “since n is even, we know there is an integer k such that n = 2k.”
  • Combine preceding results into something new. … “since n = 2k, we see that n² = 2(2k²)” or “since A ⊆ B and x ∈ A, we learn that x ∈ B.”

If you find yourself reading over a sentence that doesn't accomplish any of these goals, it is likely unnecessary and should be eliminated. … Similarly, if you find yourself doing any of these three things in a way that does not make an appearance later in the proof, it likely means it is unnecessary and that you should remove it.

Exercises: i. There are no natural numbers m and n where 2nm​=1371​ and m is odd. (The proof contains sentences such as “The fraction 2nm​ does not necessarily have to be in simplest form. We do know that 1371​ is in simplest form, though.” and “It would not be even if n = 0, though.”) ii. For all integers m and n, if m is even and n is even, then m² + n² is even. (The proof first introduces r and s with m = 2r and n = 2s, then separately introduces j and k with m² = 2j and n² = 2k.)

证明里每句话必须做三件事之一: 设立目标 (包括引理的目标); 引入新变量 (任选的或已知存在的); 把前面的结论组合出新结论. 三者都不是的句子删掉; 引入了但后面没用到的变量、设立了但没用到的中间结论也删掉. 写完初稿后专门做这一遍检查, 初稿里常有走过的弯路.

练习: (i) "分数不一定是最简形式" "1/137 是最简形式" "n = 0 时它不是偶数" 这几句后面都没用到, 删掉. (ii) r、s 引入后从没使用, 删掉这一句, 只保留 m² = 2j、n² = 2k 那条线.

变量的作用域与引入
Scope and Properly Introduce Variables

proofwriting_checklist · Page 5–6

When you use a variable in a proof, you should explicitly articulate the name of the variable, what value it represents, and where it comes from. … Every variable that you use should be of one of the following types:

  • A universally-instantiated value. A variable like this has a value that the reader of the proof chooses, but which you as the proof writer don't get to control. … Pick an even natural number n.
  • An existentially instantiated value. Sometimes, you and the reader each know that some quantity exists, but you don't know its exact value. … Since n is even, there is some integer k such that n = 2k. It's important to note that this number k is not chosen arbitrarily.
  • An explicitly chosen value. Sometimes, you'll introduce a variable simply as a simpler way of referring to some other quantity. … Let m = 2k². … Consider the set D = { x ∈ S | x ∉ f(x) }.

You might find it helpful to view a proof as a dialog between two people. … A variable whose value the reader picks. … A variable whose value you pick. … A variable whose value neither of you pick.

每个变量都要说清: 名字、代表什么、从哪里来. 来源只有三种:

  • 全称实例化: 读者任选, 作者不控制. "Pick an even natural number n."
  • 存在实例化: 双方都知道它存在, 但不知道具体值. "Since n is even, there is some integer k such that n = 2k." k 不是任选的, 只有一个 k 满足 n = 2k.
  • 明确指定: 给已有的量起个名字, 像程序里的常量. "Let m = 2k²", 康托尔定理证明里的 D = { x ∈ S | x ∉ f(x) }.

把证明看成作者和读者的对话: 读者选的、作者选的、谁也没选但大家都同意存在的. 类比 C/Java 里先声明再使用变量.

proofwriting_checklist · Page 6–7

Theorem: For any integer n, if n is even, then n² is even.

⚠ Incorrect! ⚠ Proof: For every even integer n, there exists an integer k where n = 2k. Therefore, for any even integer n and any integer k, we see that n² = (2k)² = 4k² = 2(2k²), so for any arbitrary integer m where m = 2k², we see that n² = 2m. Thus for any even integer n and integer m we see that n² = 2m, so n² is even, as required. ■

… this way of discussing n means n does not fall into any of the three aforementioned categories … If, in the course of writing a proof, you wish to make a claim that works for all choices of some value, the correct way to do it is to ask the reader to make the choice and then show the result works regardless of what that choice is. … In this proof, k should be existentially-introduced … Writing "for any arbitrary integer m where m = 2k²" makes the same mistakes as before … It's like the famous quote attributed to Henry Ford: "the customer can have any color they want as long as it's black."

Exercises: i. For all integers m and n, if m + n is even, then either m and n are even or m and n are odd. (Case 1 says “Then for all integers r and s, we have m = 2r and n = 2s + 1. … Now pick any integer t where t = r + s. …”; Case 2 says “Pick m = 137 and n = 106.”) ii. There are no nonzero real numbers x and y where xx+y​=x+yy​. (The proof says “Then for all nonzero real numbers x and y we can cross-multiply to get (x + y)² = xy.”)

错误示范的问题: "For every even integer n" 既不是让读者选, 也不是存在实例化, 也不是指定, n 的来源不明; "for any integer k" 把本该存在实例化的 k 说成任意的, 而只有一个 k 满足 n = 2k; "for any arbitrary integer m where m = 2k²" 自相矛盾, 就像福特那句「顾客可以选任何颜色, 只要是黑色」. 正确写法: "Pick an even integer n. Then there is an integer k where n = 2k. … Let m = 2k²."

练习: (i) 两个情况都错: "for all integers r and s" 应为 "there are integers r and s"; "pick any integer t where t = r + s" 应为 "let t = r + s"; 情况 2 选具体的 137 和 106 只验证了一个例子; 每个情况的结尾 "for every even integer m …" 也不对. (ii) 已经由反设得到了具体的 x 和 y, "for all nonzero real numbers x and y" 应改成 "we can cross-multiply"; 其余推理可以保留.

对具体变量作具体断言
Make Specific Claims About Specific Variables

proofwriting_checklist · Page 7–8

… statements made in a mathematical proof need to be made in reference to specific values rather than stated in the abstract. A common mistake when writing proofs is to instead describe, at a high level, why a result ought to be true, then conclude that the result is indeed true.

⚠ Incorrect! ⚠ Proof: Every divisor of a number is also a divisor of the square of that number. This means that if two divides a number, then two divides its square. Thus if n is even, then n² is even. ■

… while this proof may have some good ideas in it, it's written too abstractly to be rigorous. Unfortunately, there really isn't a way to salvage this proof.

The only way to know which of your intuitions are good and which need tuning is to explicitly validate those intuitions by attempting to formalize them mathematically.

Exercises: A natural number n is called a Hilbert number if there is a natural number k where n = 4k + 1. i. For all natural numbers m and n, if m and n are Hilbert numbers, then so is mn. (Proof: “When multiplying numbers together that have some property, the product also has that property. …”) ii. There exists a Hilbert number n > 1 such that there are Hilbert numbers p, q > 1 where n = pq. (Proof: “Since there are infinitely many pairs of Hilbert numbers we could multiply together and infinitely many Hilbert numbers, there must be some Hilbert number …”)

证明要对具体的变量做推导, 而不是泛泛地说「为什么应该成立」. 错误示范除了最后一句, 没有提到任何变量, 太抽象, 只能推倒重写. 直觉要通过形式化来检验: 能用定义一步步推出, 说明直觉对; 推不出来, 可能直觉本身就错了.

练习: (i) "有某性质的数相乘仍有该性质" 是错误的泛化 (两个素数的积不是素数). 正确做法: 设 m = 4a + 1, n = 4b + 1, 则 mn = 16ab + 4a + 4b + 1 = 4(4ab + a + b) + 1. (ii) "有无穷多对, 所以一定有" 不是证明. 直接给出: p = q = 5 (= 4·1 + 1), n = 25 = 4·6 + 1.

使用定义, 不复述定义
Don't Repeat Definitions; Use Them Instead

proofwriting_checklist · Page 8–9

Incorrect Approach 1: We know that n is even. Every even number can be written as twice some integer. Therefore, we see that n = 2k for some integer k.
Incorrect Approach 2: We know that n is even. Every even number can be written as 2k for some integer k. Therefore, we see that n = 2k for some integer k.
Incorrect Approach 3: We know that n is even. Every even number m can be written as m = 2k for some integer k. Therefore, we know that n = 2k for some integer k.

… Here's a much shorter, cleaner way to do this: We know n is even, so there is an integer k where n = 2k.

… When you're writing a proof, you should assume that the reader is familiar with all the relevant terms and definitions. … Think of it this way: the mathematical definitions we have are like the rules of a game. The proof should be you playing the game with the reader, rather than pausing every few minutes to remind the reader what the rules of the game are.

… The first one is far too general … The second one … is a variable scoping error … The third one is making specific claims about the variable m, but in that case m is a placeholder …

Exercises: i. For every odd natural number n, the sum of n and the next four natural numbers is odd. (The proof includes “An odd natural number m is one where m = 2k + 1 for some integer k.” and “An odd number is one that can be written as twice an integer plus one.”) ii. For every odd natural number a > 1, there exist natural numbers b and c where (a, b, c) is a Pythagorean triple. (The proof includes “In a Pythagorean triple, all terms must be greater than zero.”)

不要在证明里抽象地复述定义 ("每个偶数都能写成两倍的整数"), 直接把定义用在具体变量上: "n 是偶数, 所以有整数 k 使 n = 2k." 读者已知所有定义; 定义是游戏规则, 证明是和读者下棋, 不是每走几步就停下来讲规则.

复述定义还会顺带违反别的规则: 写法 1 太泛 (违反规则 ④); 写法 2 中 k 只是抽象偶数的占位符, 后面又当成具体的 k 用 (作用域错误); 写法 3 对占位符 m 作断言. 而且删掉这些句子证明会更短.

练习: (i) 删掉两句复述「奇数」定义的话即可, 计算 5n + 10 = 2(5k + 7) + 1 是对的. (ii) 删掉复述勾股三元组定义的那句 ("In a Pythagorean triple, all terms must be greater than zero."). 原证明另有两处小毛病: 等式链末尾多了一个 "$" (网页公式源码残留), "To see that b ≥ 0" 应为 b > 0.

写完整的句子和段落
Write In Complete Sentences and Paragraphs

proofwriting_checklist · Page 10–12

A good check for this is what we call the mugga mugga test. Take your proof and try reading it out loud, replacing all the mathematical content with the phrase “mugga mugga.” If what comes back is grammatically correct, then you're on the right track.

Original: Since n is even, n = 2k. · Mugga Mugga Version: Since n is even, mugga mugga.

Tip: Avoid writing sentences where mathematical notation must be treated as the verb in the sentence.

… Don't rewrite the sentence like this in order to pass the mugga mugga test: ⚠ Since n is even, n equals 2k. ⚠ … Instead, consider rewriting the sentence in a way that introduces a new subject and a new verb. … Option 1: Since n is even, we can write n = 2k. Option 2: Since n is even, we see that there is some integer k such that n = 2k. Option 3: Since n is even, there is some integer k where n = 2k.

… the word “therefore” is often abbreviated ∴, and the word “because” is often abbreviated ∵. These shorthands … should not be used in mathematical proofs …

Just as you're expected to write in complete sentences, you're expected to write in complete paragraphs. This means that your proofs should not consist of bulleted or numbered lists of statements.

Exercises: i. For all natural numbers n ≥ 1, the number n(n + 1) is not a perfect square. (The proof has lines like “n(n + 1) = k²” and “n² + n = k²” standing alone, and “So k² < (n + 1)², so k < n + 1.”) ii. 122​ is not a rational number. (This means it's not possible to precisely tune a piano.) (The proof is written with ⇒, ∴ and bare equations.)

mugga mugga 测试: 把证明大声读出来, 所有数学内容都念成 "mugga mugga", 如果剩下的句子语法通顺就合格. "Since n is even, n = 2k." 读成 "Since n is even, mugga mugga.", 没有主语和谓语, 因为谓语是等号. 规则: 不要让数学符号充当句子的谓语动词.

修法不是把 = 改写成英文 "equals" (这样丢掉了符号的精确性), 而是另加主语和谓语: "we can write n = 2k" "there is some integer k where n = 2k". 也不要用 ∴ (因此)、∵ (因为) 这类板书缩写, 不要把证明写成一条条列表, 要写成连贯的段落. 理由: 这是数学写作的通行规范, 而且逼作者把各步之间的联系写出来.

练习: (i) 单独成行的等式和 "So …, so …" 都要改成完整句子, 如 "Then n² + n = k². Notice that n² + n < (n + 1)², so k² < (n + 1)², which means k < n + 1." (ii) 去掉 ⇒、∴ 和孤立的等式, 用句子把每一步连起来: 反设 21/12=p/q, 两边取 12 次方得 2q12=p12; 令 q′=q6, p′=p6, 则 q′ 是非零整数且 2q′2=p′2, 与给定的定理 (不存在整数 p、q 使 q ≠ 0 且 p² = 2q²) 矛盾.

不用量词和联结词符号
Avoid Quantifiers and Propositional Connectives

proofwriting_checklist · Page 13

… we do not allow the use of quantifiers (∀ and ∃) or propositional connectives (→, ∧, ∨, ¬, etc.) in written proofs.

Theorem: ∀m, n ∈ ℤ. (m is even ∧ n is odd → m + n is odd)
Proof: (…) Since m is even, ∃k ∈ ℤ where m = 2k. … This means ∃s ∈ ℤ (namely, k + r) such that m + n = 2s + 1, so m + n is odd. (…) ■

Theorem: For any integers m and n, if m is even and n is odd, then m + n is odd.
Proof: (…) Since m is even, there is an integer k where m = 2k. And similarly, since n is odd, we know there's an integer r such that n = 2r + 1. … This means there is an integer s (namely, k + r) such that m + n = 2s + 1, so m + n is odd. (…) ■

Notice also that our corrected version of the proof still has algebraic symbols (such as =, +, −, and so on). Those are perfectly acceptable …

书面证明里不用 ∀、∃ 和 →、∧、∨、¬. 这些符号是一阶逻辑的工具, 用来在写证明之前精确表达和变形命题 (例如求否定), 证明本身要写成英文. 代数符号 (=、+、−) 可以用, 只要句子通过 mugga mugga 测试. 理由: 规范如此, 而且大段符号逻辑比英文更难读、更易出错.

避免反证三明治
Avoid the “Contradiction Sandwich”

proofwriting_checklist · Page 14–16

⚠ (Poor Style!) ⚠ Proof: Assume for the sake of contradiction that there are integers m and n where m is even, n is odd, but m + n is even. Since m is even, there is an integer k where m = 2k. … so m + n is odd. But this is impossible, since earlier we assumed that m + n is even. We've reached a contradiction …

Because the core line of reasoning in this proof works just as well as a direct proof, we call the original proof a contradiction sandwich. Essentially, the proof proceeds like this:

  1. Assume, for the sake of contradiction, that the theorem is false.
  2. Prove the theorem using a direct proof.
  3. This contradicts that the theorem is false, so the theorem is true.

… if you finish writing a proof by contradiction, take a minute or two to read over your proof. Is it a contradiction sandwich? If so, simply remove the contradiction bits and present the direct proof on its own.

Exercises: i. For all real numbers a and b, we have |a + b| ≤ |a| + |b|. (Proof by contradiction whose cases show |a + b| ≤ |a| + |b| directly.) ii. For all integers n, if n² is even, then n is even. (Assume n² is even but n is odd; show n² = 2m + 1 is odd. “We have reached a contradiction, or our assumption was wrong …”)

contradiction sandwich 反证三明治: 反设定理不成立 → 中间其实完整地直接证明了定理 → 说这与反设矛盾. 逻辑上没错, 但首尾两片「面包」什么也没贡献. 写完反证法后检查一下, 如果是三明治, 就去掉反证的部分, 改成直接证明. 这不是说不该用反证法.

练习: (i) 是三明治: 中间分两种情况已直接证出 |a + b| ≤ |a| + |b|, 去掉首尾即可. (ii) 是「逆否三明治」: 中间证的是 "n 是奇数 ⟹ n² 是奇数", 应改写成逆否证明. 结尾 "or our assumption was wrong" 的 or 是 so 的笔误.

否定指南与逻辑翻译指南
Guide to Negation · Guide to Logic Translation

guide_to_negation · guide_to_translation · Page 1

Guide to Negation — This animated guide explains how to negate formulas in propositional and first-order logic. Guide to Negation

Guide to Logic Translation — This animated guide explains how to translate English statements into first-order logic. Guide to Logic Translations

这两页只是两份动画指南 (PDF 幻灯片) 的入口: 一份讲如何对命题逻辑和一阶逻辑公式取否定, 一份讲如何把英文句子翻译成一阶逻辑. 内容对应 CS103 03、04、05.

取否定的规则汇总 (课上讲过, 动画指南按这些规则一步步把 ¬ 推到最里层):

公式否定
¬(P∧Q)¬P∨¬Q
¬(P∨Q)¬P∧¬Q
¬(P→Q)P∧¬Q
¬(P↔Q)P↔¬Q
¬∀x. P(x)∃x. ¬P(x)
¬∃x. P(x)∀x. ¬P(x)

翻译的核心是四种亚里士多德形式: "所有 P 都是 Q" ∀x.(P(x)→Q(x)); "有 P 是 Q" ∃x.(P(x)∧Q(x)); "没有 P 是 Q" ∀x.(P(x)→¬Q(x)); "有 P 不是 Q" ∃x.(P(x)∧¬Q(x)). 下面的检查清单就是在这两份指南的基础上写的.

一阶逻辑翻译检查清单
First-Order Translation Checklist

fol_checklist · Page 1

Although first-order logic is a system used to precisely describe worlds and define various terms, in many ways it feels like a little mini programming language built into mathematics. It has variables, things that work like loops (the ∀ and ∃ quantifiers), etc. As a result, we figured it would be worth putting together the equivalent of a “style guide” for that programming language.

Here's the checklist we recommend you run through when working on logic translations:

  • Check the types of all terms in the formula.
  • Check the scoping on each variable.
  • Pair quantifiers with the appropriate connectives.
  • Use whitespace and indentation to clarify meaning.
  • Defer quantifiers until they're needed.

一阶逻辑像数学里的一门小编程语言: 有变量, 量词 ∀、∃ 像循环. 所以这份清单相当于它的「代码风格指南」, 目标是让公式更易读、便于排错, 并从方法上减少出错. 五条: 检查类型; 检查变量作用域; 量词与联结词正确搭配; 用空白和缩进表达结构; 量词用到时再引入.

检查类型
Check the Types of All Terms in the Formula

fol_checklist · Page 1–2

First-order logic draws a distinction between objects and truth values. All variables in first-order logic represent objects, and predicates applied to those functions produce truth values. You can only apply predicates or functions to objects, and you can only apply connectives or quantifiers to truth values.

… Start off by finding all the objects or variables in the formula. For each of them, mark them as type object. Then find the functions. The inputs to any function must also have type object, and the overall function evaluates to something of type object. Then find the predicates – their inputs must all be objects, and their output is of type truth value. Finally, look at quantifiers and propositional connectives. Their inputs must have type truth value, and their outputs are of type truth value as well.

Predicates Puppy(x), Cute(x), Person(x); function OwnerOf(x). “everyone owns at least one cute puppy”:

⚠ Incorrect Translation ⚠ ∀p. (Person(p)=OwnerOf(∃d. (Puppy(d)∧Cute(d))))

⚠ Incorrect Translation ⚠ ∀p. (Person(p)→∃d. (OwnerOf(Cute(Puppy(d)))=p))

Exercises: i. The following is a valid first-order logic formula. Knowing that it's valid, determine which terms are functions and which are predicates. ∀x. (P(x)=Q(R(x))→∃y. (S(x,y)↔T(x,U(y)))) ii. … "all people who wear hats love all people who don't wear hats." … ∀p. (WearsHat(Person(p))→∀q. Loves(p,¬WearsHat(Person(q))))

一阶逻辑区分两种类型: 对象和真值. 变量、函数值是对象; 谓词作用于对象, 得到真值; 联结词和量词只作用于真值, 结果也是真值; 等号 = 只能比较两个对象. 提交前逐项「类型检查」, 就像 C++ 里不能拿字符串和整数比较.

两个错误翻译: 第一个用 = 比较 Person(p) (真值) 和 OwnerOf(…), 还把函数 OwnerOf 用在量化式 ∃d. … (真值) 上; 第二个把谓词 Cute 用在 Puppy(d) (真值) 上. 正确翻译: ∀p. (Person(p)→∃d. (Puppy(d)∧Cute(d)∧OwnerOf(d)=p)).

练习: (i) = 两边必须是对象, 所以 P、Q、R 都是函数; S、T 在 ↔ 两边, 是谓词; U(y) 是 T 的参数, 是函数. (ii) Person(p) 是真值, 不能传给 WearsHat; ¬WearsHat(…) 是真值, 不能传给 Loves. 改为 ∀p. (Person(p)∧WearsHat(p)→∀q. (Person(q)∧¬WearsHat(q)→Loves(p,q))).

检查变量作用域
Check the Scoping on Each Variable

fol_checklist · Page 2–3

There are two general classes of scoping mistakes we see people make. The first one is to omit an important pair of parentheses. … “there is a movie featuring both Emma Stone and Ryan Gosling.”

⚠ Incorrect Translation ⚠ ∃m. Movie(m)∧AppearsIn(EmmaStone,m)∧AppearsIn(RyanGosling,m)

… existential quantifiers have high operator precedence – higher than anything else, in fact – so this expression is interpreted as (∃m. Movie(m))∧(AppearsIn(EmmaStone,m))∧(AppearsIn(RyanGosling,m)) … As a rule of thumb, any time you introduce a quantifier, surround the expression you want to quantify with parentheses.

The other scoping error we typically see involves quantifying over a variable at the wrong time. … “every person has a puppy”:

⚠ Incorrect Trnslation ⚠ ∃d. (Puppy(d))∧∀p. (Person(p)→HasPet(p,d))

Correct Formula ∀p. (Person(p)→∃d. (Puppy(d)∧HasPet(p,d)))

Exercises: i. "there is a robot that loves itself, a cat that loves itself, and that robot loves that cat." ∃r. Robot(r)∧Loves(r,r)∧∃c. Cat(c)∧Loves(c,c)∧Loves(r,c) ii. "there's a robot that loves all cats, and every person loves that robot." ∃r. (Robot(r)∧∀c. (Cat(c)→Loves(r,c)))∧∀p. (Person(p)→∃r. Loves(p,r))

作用域错误有两类. ① 漏括号: 量词的优先级最高, ∃m. Movie(m)∧… 只量化了 Movie(m), 后面的 m 已出作用域, 就像在 C++ 的块外使用局部变量. 经验法则: 每引入一个量词, 就用括号把它要管的整个式子括起来. ② 量词放错位置: "每个人都有一只小狗" 把 ∃d 放在最外层并且括号提前闭合, HasPet(p, d) 里的 d 出了作用域; 而且即使括号对了, 意思也变成「有一只小狗是所有人的宠物」. 应把 ∃d 嵌在 ∀p 里面, 先谈到某个人, 再谈他的小狗.

练习: (i) 加括号: ∃r. (Robot(r)∧Loves(r,r)∧∃c. (Cat(c)∧Loves(c,c)∧Loves(r,c))). (ii) 后面的 r 是新引入的另一个变量, 和前面的机器人无关, 而且第一个 r 的括号已闭合. 改为 ∃r. (Robot(r)∧∀c. (Cat(c)→Loves(r,c))∧∀p. (Person(p)→Loves(p,r))).

原文笔误: "Incorrect Trnslation" 应为 Translation.

量词与联结词的搭配
Pair Quantifiers With the Appropriate Connectives

fol_checklist · Page 3–5

… Those forms pair the → connective with the ∀ quantifier and the ∧ connective with the ∃ quantifier. … mixing up the → and ∧ connectives and pairing them with the wrong quantifier is one of the single most common mistakes we see …

“there's a horse with no name:” ⚠ Incorrect Translation ⚠ ∃h. (Horse(h)→∀n. (NameOf(h)=n)) … this first-order logic formula would be true: just choose as h something that isn't a horse.

“everybody has someone to lean on:” ⚠ Incorrect Translation ⚠ ∀p. (Person(p)∧∃q. (Person(p)∧CanLeanOn(p,q))) … pick as p something that isn't a person (say, Mt. Everest). Then Person(p) is false … so the overall formula is false.

“there is someone that everybody else loves” Correct Formula ∃p. (Person(p)∧∀q. (Person(q)∧q=p→Loves(q,p))) … remember that the ∧ connective has higher precedence than →, so the grouping here is ∀q. ((Person(q)∧q=p)→(…))

… You will also sometimes see ∃ paired with ↔ … Correct Formula ∃S. (Set(S)∧∀x. (x∈S↔x=137)) (Question to ponder: what does this say?) If we negate this formula and push the negation as deep as possible, we get this statement: ∀S. (Set(S)→∃x. (x∈S↔x=137))

A great specific test you can do check if your formulas have the right quantifiers is to use the “Mount Everest” test that we did in class.

Exercises: i. ∃c. (Cat(c)→∀r. (Robot(r)∧Loves(c,r))) ii. ∀r. (Robot(r)∧Loves(r,r)→∀c. (Cat(c)∧Loves(c,c)∧Loves(c,r)∧Loves(r,c)→∃p. (Person(p)∧Loves(r,p)∧Loves(c,p)))) — Are the quantifiers in this statement paired with the correct connectives?

规则: ∀ 配 →, ∃ 配 ∧. 搭错是最常见的错误之一. 检验方法是「珠穆朗玛峰测试」: 把量化变量取成一个完全不相干的东西 (珠峰), 看会不会意外让整个公式变真或变假.

  • ∃ 配 →: "有一匹没有名字的马" 被翻译成 ∃h.(Horse(h) → …), 取 h = 珠峰, 前件为假, 蕴涵为真, 公式在任何世界都为真.
  • ∀ 配 ∧: "每个人都有可依靠的人" 被翻译成 ∀p.(Person(p) ∧ …), 取 p = 珠峰, Person(p) 为假, 公式在任何世界都为假.

看似例外的情况: ∀q.(Person(q) ∧ q ≠ p → …) 里 ∧ 优先于 →, 顶层仍是 →, 没有违反规则. 集合论里常见 ∀ 配 ↔ (外延公理式的写法); 对它取否定会得到 ∃ 配 ↔, 因为 ¬(p ↔ q) 等价于 p ↔ ¬q, ↔ 否定后还是 ↔. 原文的思考题: 第一个公式说「存在一个集合, 其元素恰好是 137」, 即 {137} 存在; 否定说「每个集合都不等于 {137}」.

练习: (i) 两处都搭错了: ∃ 配了 →, ∀ 配了 ∧. 应为 ∃c. (Cat(c)∧∀r. (Robot(r)→Loves(c,r))). (ii) 全部正确: 两个 ∀ 的顶层联结词都是 → (∧ 优先级更高), ∃ 配 ∧.

用空白和缩进
Use Whitespace and Indentation to Clarify Meaning

fol_checklist · Page 5–6

… “every nonempty tournament has a tournament champion:”

∀T. (Tournament(T) ∧ (∃p. p ∈ T) →
  ∃c. (c ∈ T ∧
    ∀p. (p ∈ T ∧ c ≠ p →
      (Beat(c, p) ∨ ∃q ∈ T. (Beat(c, q) ∧ Beat(q, p)))
    )
  )
)

It's a good execise to see why this works. As a hint, the general pattern is the following: For any tournament T that has at least one player, There is a player c (our champion) in T where For any player p in the tournament other than c, Either c beat p or c beat some player q who in turn beat p.

⚠ Please Don't Do This! ⚠ (the same formula on a single line) … This is the mathematical equivalent of writing a program like this one:

int main(){for(int i=0;i<5;i++){for(int j=0;j<5;j++){cout<<(i*j)<<endl;}}return 0;}

简单公式写一行没问题, 复杂公式要分行并按嵌套层次缩进. 例子: "每个非空锦标赛都有冠军" (冠军 c: 对其他每个选手 p, 要么 c 直接赢了 p, 要么 c 赢了某个赢过 p 的 q; 见 CS103 04 的锦标赛). 分行缩进后, 每一层都对应一个亚里士多德形式, 一眼能读出意思; 挤在一行里连括号是否配对都难查, 就像把整个 C++ 程序写成一行. 公式往往要反复修改, 缩进好的公式改起来容易得多.

原文中 "execise" 是 "exercise" 的笔误.

量词用到时再引入
Defer Quantifiers Until They're Needed

fol_checklist · Page 6–8

In most programming languages, you have the option to declare variables at many different points in a function. It's generally considered a good idea to declare variables as late as you possibly can. … In first-order logic, you have the ability to introduce variables at different points in a formula by using quantifiers. Our advice to you is the same as in programming: don't put all the quantifiers at the front of the formula.

“there's a kitten that loves everyone.” ⚠ Incorrect Translation ⚠ ∃k. ∀p. (Kitten(k)∧Person(p)→Loves(k,p)) … this gets parsed as follows: ∃k. ∀p. ((Kitten(k)∧Person(p))→Loves(k,p)) … imagine that we pick k to be something that isn't a kitten. That choice of k makes the entire formula true.

Correct Formula ∃k. (Kitten(k)∧∀p. (Person(p)→Loves(k,p)))

… introduce quantifiers one at a time and only at the specific point in which you actually need them. … (Pro tip / life advice: you should not feel good about anything you do that is technically correct or technically legal.)

Exercises: i. "for every robot, there is a cat that loves exactly the same people as that robot." ∀r. ∃c. ∀p. (Robot(r)∧Cat(c)∧Person(p)→(Loves(r,p)↔Loves(c,p))) ii. "every nonempty finite set of natural numbers has a greatest element." ∀S. ∀n. ∀k. ∃m. ∀x. (Set(S)∧n∈S→n∈N∧k∈N∧k>0∧∣S∣=k∧m∈S∧x∈S∧x=m→x<m)

编程中变量要尽量晚声明: 从声明位置就能看出它是整个循环都要用的、循环计数器、还是每轮临时的, 也不容易读到未初始化或上一轮残留的值. 一阶逻辑同理: 不要把所有量词都堆在最前面.

例子: "有一只爱所有人的小猫" 若写成 ∃k.∀p.(Kitten(k) ∧ Person(p) → …), 实际上是 ∃ 包着一个蕴涵, 取 k = 不是小猫的东西, 前件为假, 公式恒真. 把 ∀p 推迟到 Kitten(k) 之后, 就自然得到 ∃ 配 ∧ 的正确形式. 即使量词全放前面碰巧对了, 也不是好风格.

练习: (i) ∀r. (Robot(r)→∃c. (Cat(c)∧∀p. (Person(p)→(Loves(r,p)↔Loves(c,p))))); 原式同样有 ∃c 配 → 的问题. (ii) 先写前提「S 是集合, 元素都是自然数, 大小是正自然数」, 再写结论「有最大元」:

∀S. (Set(S) ∧ ∀n. (n ∈ S → n ∈ ℕ) ∧ ∃k. (k ∈ ℕ ∧ k > 0 ∧ |S| = k) →
  ∃m. (m ∈ S ∧
    ∀x. (x ∈ S ∧ x ≠ m → x < m)
  )
)

原文排版问题: "the existential statement wraps a statement whose top-level connective is ⊤" 中的符号应为 ∧ (网页渲染出错); 前文 "use the check" 应为 "use to check", "you can do check" 应为 "you can do to check".

集合证明指南
Guide to Proofs on Sets

guide_to_proofs_on_sets · Page 1

What Folks Get Wrong

By far the most common mistake people make when writing proofs about sets is to operate at the wrong level of detail. Because sets represent groups of things, you might think that a proof about a set would talk holistically about what sorts of objects are in the set and why those objects meet certain requirements. However, that's not what a proof about sets actually looks like. Instead, proofs on sets almost always involve working with individual, arbitrarily-chosen elements of the sets in question.

To formalize your intuition about sets and how they behave … you'll want to shift your thinking from a holistic “A ∪ B represents the set you get when you combine A and B together” to a more precise “x ∈ A ∪ B if and only if x ∈ A or x ∈ B.”

集合证明最常见的错误是细节层次不对: 整体地描述集合里有什么样的对象、为什么满足要求. 真正的集合证明几乎总是针对任选的单个元素来写, 就像全称命题的证明围绕一个任选的值展开. 思路要从「A ∪ B 是把 A 和 B 合起来」转到「x ∈ A ∪ B 当且仅当 x ∈ A 或 x ∈ B」, 从集合整体的性质转到单个元素的性质. 直觉可以用整体描述来建立, 但证明的写法完全不同.

大表
The Big Table

guide_to_proofs_on_sets · Page 1–2
StatementDefinitionIf you assume this is true…To prove this is true…
S⊆T∀x∈S. x∈TInitially, do nothing. Once you find some z ∈ S, conclude z ∈ T.Ask the reader to pick an x ∈ S. Then prove x ∈ T.
S=TS⊆T∧T⊆SAssume S ⊆ T and T ⊆ S. Or, equivalently, initially, do nothing. If you find an z ∈ S you can conclude z ∈ T and vice-versa.Prove S ⊆ T and T ⊆ S.
S=TS⊆T∨T⊆SConsider two cases: Case 1: There exists an x ∈ S where x ∉ T. Case 2: There exists an x ∈ T where x ∉ S.Prove there exists an x where either x ∈ S and x ∉ T, or x ∉ S and x ∈ T.
x∈A∩Bx∈A∧x∈BAssume x ∈ A. Also assume x ∈ B.Prove x ∈ A. Also prove x ∈ B.
x∈A∪Bx∈A∨x∈BConsider two cases: Case 1: x ∈ A. Case 2: x ∈ B.Either prove x ∈ A or prove x ∈ B.
x∈A−Bx∈A∧x∈/BAssume x ∈ A. Also assume x ∉ B.Prove x ∈ A. Also prove x ∉ B.
