A∈℘(B)A⊆BAssume A ⊆ B.Prove A ⊆ B.
x∈{y∣P(y)}P(x)Assume P(x).Prove P(x).

集合证明的总原则是回到形式定义. 这张表要背下来: 每一行给出一个命题的定义, 以及假设它成立时能做什么、要证明它时要做什么. 最常用的几行:

  • 证 S ⊆ T: 让读者任选 x ∈ S, 证 x ∈ T. 假设 S ⊆ T: 先什么都不做, 等手上出现 S 的某个元素时, 再用它得出该元素属于 T.
  • 证 S = T: 证两个方向的 ⊆. 证 S ≠ T: 找一个只在其中一个集合里的元素.
  • ∩ 对应「且」(两件事都假设 / 都证明); ∪ 对应「或」(假设时分情况, 证明时证其一); A − B 是「在 A 且不在 B」; 对称差 A Δ B 是「恰在其中一个」.
  • A ∈ ℘(B) 就是 A ⊆ B, 幂集让 ∈ 和 ⊆ 互相转换.
  • x ∈ { y | P(y) } 就是 P(x); 占位变量 y 消失.
guide_to_proofs_on_sets · Page 2–3

First, notice that this table never actually gives a formal definition to what A ∪ B is, or what A − B means, etc. Instead, it talks about what x ∈ A ∪ B means … The rules governing how x ∈ A ∪ B behaves gives an operational definition to A ∪ B. An operational definition is a way of defining an object by describing how it behaves and what its properties are, rather than saying what specifically it is. A good example of this is cube roots. We can define the cube root of x to be the real number y where y³ = x. … this definition is not going to give you an algorithm for figuring out what 37​ is.

Next, notice that the statements A = B and A ≠ B have definitions given in the table. … It's common to think that proving A = B when A and B are sets requires arguing that the two collections have the same elements, perhaps by describing how the sets are formed and what they contain. But the mathematical requirements of proving two sets are equal operate at a much lower level than this, focusing instead on the subset-of relation.

Finally, let's look at the very last row of this table … the set { n | n ∈ ℕ ∧ n is even } is the set of all even natural numbers, the set { S | S ⊆ ℕ } is the set of all subsets of ℕ …, and the set { x | x ∈ ℝ ∧ x² = 4 } is the set of all numbers whose square is 4 … Notice in this discussion that the variable used on the left-hand side of the set-builder notation … are just placeholders. … the statement m ∈ { n | n ∈ ℕ ∧ n is even } is basically a fancy way of saying that m ∈ ℕ and m is even. There is no discussion of n at all in this - the placeholder goes away as soon as we start talking about a concrete object.

三点说明. ① 表里没说 A ∪ B「是什么」, 只说了 x ∈ A ∪ B 的含义, 这就是 operational definition 操作性定义: 用对象的行为和性质来定义它, 而不是给出它本身. 类比立方根: "满足 y³ = x 的实数 y" 告诉你 2 是 8 的立方根, 却不告诉你怎么算 ∛7.

② 证两个集合相等不是描述它们怎样构成、含有什么, 而是证明互为子集, 层次更低.

③ 集合构造式左边的变量只是占位符: { n | n ∈ ℕ ∧ n 是偶数 } 里没有一个叫 n 的数. m 属于这个集合, 意思就是 m 是偶自然数, n 不再出现.

基本集合运算的证明
Proofs on Core Set Operations

guide_to_proofs_on_sets · Page 3–6

Theorem: If A and B are sets, then A ∩ B = A if and only if A ⊆ B.

Proof: Pick any sets A and B. We will prove each direction of implication separately.

(⇒) Assume that A ∩ B = A. We need to show that A ⊆ B. To do so, pick some x ∈ A. We will prove that x ∈ B. Since x ∈ A and A ∩ B = A, we learn that x ∈ A ∩ B. And since x ∈ A ∩ B, we see that x ∈ B, which is what we needed to show.

(⇐) Assume that A ⊆ B. We need to show that A ∩ B = A. To do so, we need to prove both that A ∩ B ⊆ A and that A ⊆ A ∩ B.

First, we'll prove that A ∩ B ⊆ A. To that end, choose some x ∈ A ∩ B, and we'll prove that x ∈ A. Because x ∈ A ∩ B, we see that x ∈ A, which is what we needed to show.

Next, we'll prove that A ⊆ A ∩ B. So pick some x ∈ A, and we'll prove that x ∈ A ∩ B. We know that x ∈ A and A ⊆ B, which means we know x ∈ B. Then, since x ∈ A and x ∈ B, we know that x ∈ A ∩ B, which is what we needed to show. ■

Notice how our proof hinges extensively on asking the reader to pick elements of the relevant sets and then focusing just on those elements. … Also notice how instead of trying to take aim at a general pattern, we instead slowly and methodically expanded out definitions one after the other until we arrived at the result we wanted.

指南一步步搭出这个证明, 这里只录最终版. 搭建过程的思路:

  1. 定理是双条件, 先写骨架: 任选集合 A、B, 两个方向分别证.
  2. (⇒) 假设 A ∩ B = A, 查表: 先不动, 等出现 A 或 A ∩ B 的元素. 目标 A ⊆ B, 查表: 让读者任选 x ∈ A, 目标变成 x ∈ B.
  3. 现在手上有 x ∈ A, 用上等式得 x ∈ A ∩ B, 再按 ∩ 的定义拆出 x ∈ B, 完成.
  4. (⇐) 目标 A ∩ B = A 拆成两个 ⊆. A ∩ B ⊆ A: 任选 x ∈ A ∩ B, 直接拆出 x ∈ A (x ∈ B 用不到就不写). A ⊆ A ∩ B: 任选 x ∈ A, 这时等待已久的假设 A ⊆ B 派上用场, 得 x ∈ B, 合起来 x ∈ A ∩ B.

要点: 不是一眼看出整体规律, 而是按表把定义一层层展开, 直到结论出现.

幂集的证明
Proofs on Power Sets

guide_to_proofs_on_sets · Page 6–7

Theorem: If S ⊆ ℘(S), then ℘(S) ⊆ ℘(℘(S)).

… You might be tempted to think this is true about all sets - aren't all sets contained in their power set? - but that's not quite what this says. The statement S ∈ ℘(S) is true for all sets S because each set is a subset of itself, but we're looking at S ⊆ ℘(S), not S ∈ ℘(S).

How about ∅? That will work, since ∅ is a subset of every set. How about {137}? That will not work. Its power set is {∅, {137}}, and {137} ⊈ {∅, {137}} because 137 ∈ {137} but 137 ∉ {∅, {137}}. … any set S containing a non-set element can't satisfy S ⊆ ℘(S). … Let's try, then {{137}}. … the only element of {{137}} is {137}, and {137} ⊈ {{137}}. … With a little trial and error, you might find the set S = {∅}. … You could also find S = {∅, {∅}} works, and in fact there's infinitely many sets that work here.

More generally, if we pause and look at what S ⊆ ℘(S) means, it intuitively means "every element of S is a subset of S."

先读懂前提 S ⊆ ℘(S). 对所有集合成立的是 S ∈ ℘(S) (每个集合是自身的子集), 而 S ⊆ ℘(S) 说的是「S 的每个元素都是 S 的子集」(因为 X ∈ ℘(S) 等价于 X ⊆ S). 试例子:

  • ∅: 成立, 空集是任何集合的子集.
  • {137}: 不成立, 137 不是集合, 不可能是任何集合的子集. 所以含有非集合元素的 S 都不行.
  • {{137}}: 不成立, 唯一元素 {137} 不是 {{137}} 的子集 (137 ∉ {{137}}).
  • {∅}、{∅, {∅}}: 成立, 而且这样的集合有无穷多个 (集合论里叫传递集).
guide_to_proofs_on_sets · Page 7–9

Proof: Assume S is a set where S ⊆ ℘(S). We need to prove that ℘(S) ⊆ ℘(℘(S)).

Choose some X ∈ ℘(S). We will show that X ∈ ℘(℘(S)), or, equivalently, that X ⊆ ℘(S). So pick some Y ∈ X; we will then show that Y ∈ ℘(S). Because X ∈ ℘(S), we know that X ⊆ S. And since Y ∈ X and X ⊆ S, we know that Y ∈ S. Finally, since Y ∈ S and S ⊆ ℘(S), we see that Y ∈ ℘(S), which is what we needed to show. ■

There are a few important details to note about this proof. First, notice how power sets let us switch between the ∈ and ⊆ relationship. … Next, notice how we ended up with two new variables in our proof that weren't in the statement of the theorem. … Third, notice that at several points in this proof, we had multiple choices about how to proceed, and it wasn't clear which one to pick. … And finally, notice how midway through our proof, we realized that our organization was getting a bit messy and adjusted accordingly.

证明的展开过程: 目标 ℘(S) ⊆ ℘(℘(S)) → 任选 X ∈ ℘(S), 目标 X ∈ ℘(℘(S)), 即 X ⊆ ℘(S) → 任选 Y ∈ X, 目标 Y ∈ ℘(S). 已知方面: X ∈ ℘(S) 给出 X ⊆ S; Y ∈ X 且 X ⊆ S 给出 Y ∈ S; 最后 Y ∈ S 且 S ⊆ ℘(S) 给出 Y ∈ ℘(S), 正是目标.

四点体会: ① 幂集让 ∈ 和 ⊆ 来回转换; ② X、Y 两个新变量不是事先猜出来的, 是按表展开定义时自然「掉出来」的, 用大写字母是因为它们都是集合; ③ 中途有多条路可走 (把 Y ∈ ℘(S) 改写成 Y ⊆ S, 还是用 S ⊆ ℘(S)), 选择需要试探, 能直接到达目标的一步优先; ④ 写到一半发现第一段既写目标又写推理, 就重新组织成「先列全部目标, 再推理」.

原文笔误: 指南在搭建这个证明时有三处写错 (最终版是对的): 展开 X ∈ ℘(S) 时写 "we should assume that X ⊆ A", 应为 X ⊆ S; 中间稿的占位写 "(… proof that S ⊆ ℘(S) goes here …)", 应为 X ⊆ ℘(S); 另一稿写 "prove that Y ∈ ℘(X)", 应为 Y ∈ ℘(S).

集合构造式的证明
Proofs on Set-Builder Notation

guide_to_proofs_on_sets · Page 9–11

Theorem: Let f:℘(N)→℘(N) be defined as f(S)={n∣n∈S∧∃k∈N. n=3k+1}. Then if A, B ∈ ℘(ℕ) and A ⊆ B, then f(A) ⊆ f(B).

… we see that f is a function that takes in a set of natural numbers and outputs a set of natural numbers. … it seems like this says "start with the set S, then filter it down to just those numbers n that can be written as 3k + 1 for some natural number k." So, for example, we'd have f({1, 2, 3}) = {1}, and we'd have f({1, 3, 7}) = {1, 7}.

Proof: Pick any sets A, B ∈ ℘(ℕ) such that A ⊆ B. We need to prove that f(A) ⊆ f(B). So choose some m ∈ f(A); we need to show that m ∈ f(B).

Since we have m ∈ f(A), we know that m ∈ A and that there is some k ∈ ℕ such that m = 3k + 1. Then, since m ∈ A and A ⊆ B, we see that m ∈ B. Collectively, we see that m = 3k + 1 and that m ∈ B, so m ∈ f(B), as required. ■

先读懂 f: 定义域和陪域都是 ℘(ℕ), 所以 f 输入一个自然数集合、输出一个自然数集合. f(S) 是把 S 过滤到只剩形如 3k + 1 的数, 如 f({1, 2, 3}) = {1}, f({1, 3, 7}) = {1, 7}. 定理的直觉: A ⊆ B 时, 两者各自过滤后仍保持包含关系.

证明: 目标是 ⊆, 任选 m ∈ f(A). 按大表最后一行, m ∈ f(A) 就是 "m ∈ A 且存在 k 使 m = 3k + 1" (占位变量 n 不出现). 目标 m ∈ f(B) 同样展开为 "m ∈ B 且存在 k 使 m = 3k + 1"; 后半已有, 前半由 m ∈ A 和 A ⊆ B 得到.

原文笔误: 推导中写 "we should conclude that m ∈ B and that there's a k ∈ ℕ where m = 3k + 1", 应为 m ∈ A (由 m ∈ f(A) 只能得到 m ∈ A; 下一句的证明稿里写的就是 m ∈ A).

练习
Exercises

guide_to_proofs_on_sets · Page 11
  1. Let A, B, and C be sets. Prove that A ∪ (B ∩ C) = (A ∪ B) ∩ (A ∪ C).
  2. Let A and B be sets. Prove that (A Δ B) Δ B = A.
  3. Let A and B be sets. Prove that ℘(A) − ℘(B) ≠ ℘(A − B).
  4. Let A and B be sets. Prove that ℘(A ∩ B) = ℘(A) ∩ ℘(B).
  5. Consider the function f:℘(℘(N))→℘(N) defined as f(S)={x∣∃T∈S. x∈T}. Prove that for all X, Y ∈ ℘(℘(ℕ)) that f(X ∪ Y) ⊆ f(X) ∪ f(Y).
  6. If f : A → B is a function and S ⊆ A, then the image of S under f, denoted f[S], is the set f[S] = { b | ∃a ∈ S. f(a) = b }. Let f : A → A be an involution. Prove for all sets S ⊆ A that f[f[S]] = S.

答案思路 (都按大表展开):

  1. 两个方向的 ⊆. 左 ⊆ 右: 任选 x, 分 x ∈ A 和 x ∈ B ∩ C 两种情况, 两种都得到 x ∈ A ∪ B 且 x ∈ A ∪ C. 右 ⊆ 左: 若 x ∈ A 直接成立; 否则由 x ∈ A ∪ B 得 x ∈ B, 由 x ∈ A ∪ C 得 x ∈ C.
  2. 任选 x, 按 x 是否属于 A、B 分四种情况检查 (A Δ B) Δ B 的隶属, 结果都与 x ∈ A 一致. 直觉: 和 B 做两次对称差, B 的影响抵消.
  3. 找一个只在一边的元素: ∅ ∈ ℘(A − B), 但 ∅ ∈ ℘(B), 所以 ∅ ∉ ℘(A) − ℘(B). 这对任何 A、B 都成立.
  4. X ∈ ℘(A ∩ B) ⟺ X ⊆ A ∩ B ⟺ X ⊆ A 且 X ⊆ B ⟺ X ∈ ℘(A) 且 X ∈ ℘(B). 写成证明时中间一步要按元素展开.
  5. f(S) 是 S 中所有集合的并. 任选 x ∈ f(X ∪ Y), 则有 T ∈ X ∪ Y 使 x ∈ T; 分 T ∈ X (得 x ∈ f(X)) 和 T ∈ Y (得 x ∈ f(Y)) 两种情况.
  6. involution 对合: f(f(a)) = a. ⊆: 任选 b ∈ f[f[S]], 有 c ∈ f[S] 使 f(c) = b, 又有 a ∈ S 使 f(a) = c, 于是 b = f(f(a)) = a ∈ S. ⊇: 任选 s ∈ S, f(s) ∈ f[S], 而 f(f(s)) = s, 所以 s ∈ f[f[S]].

离散结构证明指南
Guide to Proofs on Discrete Structures

guide_to_proofs_on_discrete_structures · Page 1

… The new skill you'll need to sharpen for this problem set is determining how to start with a statement like “prove that f is an injection” and to figure out what exactly it is that you're supposed to be doing. … While you're welcome to just steal these proof setups for your own use, we recommend that you focus more on the process by which these templates were developed …

This page is divided into four parts.

  • The Big Tables, which explains what you can assume and what you can prove about different first-order logic constructs;
  • Proof Templates, which use The Big Tables to show how to structure proofs of definitions specified in first-order logic;
  • Defining Things, which explains how to define mathematical objects of different types; and
  • Writing Longer Proofs, which explains how to write proofs that feel just a little bit longer than the ones we've done so far.

函数、图等离散结构的定义都用一阶逻辑写成, 新技能是: 拿到 "证明 f 是单射" 这样的题, 看清到底要做什么. 证明的一般原则不变. 指南分四部分: 两张大表 (证明和假设各种一阶逻辑结构时分别怎么做)、证明模板、如何定义对象、如何写较长的证明. 模板可以照抄, 但更重要的是理解模板是怎么从定义推出来的, 因为后面会不断遇到新定义. 对应 CS103 06、07.

大表: 证明与假设
The Big Tables

guide_to_proofs_on_discrete_structures · Page 1–2

Proving Statements

ProvingHow
∀x. PDirect proof: Pick an arbitrary x, then prove that P is true for that choice of x. By contradiction: Suppose for the sake of contradiction that there exists some x where P is false. Then derive a contradiction.
∃x. PDirect proof: Do some exploring and find a choice of x where P is true. Then, write a proof defining x explaining why P is true in that case. (Proofs by contradiction of existential statements are extremely rare.)
¬PDirect proof: Simplify your formula by pushing the negation deeper, then apply the appropriate rule. By contradiction: Suppose for the sake of contradiction that P is true, then derive a contradiction.
P ∧ QDirect proof: Prove each of P and Q independently. By contradiction: Assume ¬P ∨ ¬Q. Then, try to derive a contradiction.
P ∨ QDirect proof: Prove that ¬P → Q, or prove that ¬Q → P. (Great question to ponder: why does this work? You might want to look at the truth tables.) Alternatively, either prove P or prove Q. By contradiction: Assume ¬P ∧ ¬Q. Then, try to derive a contradiction.
P → QDirect proof: Assume P is true, then prove Q. By contradiction: Assume P is true and Q is false, then derive a contradiction. By contrapositive: Assume ¬Q, then prove ¬P.
P ↔ QProve both P → Q and Q → P.

证明各种结构的方法: ∀ 让读者任选, 再证; ∃ 自己找出对象, 再验证 (存在命题很少用反证); ¬P 先把否定推进去再按对应规则; ∧ 两个分别证; ∨ 证 "¬P → Q" 或 "¬Q → P", 或直接证其一; → 直接、反证、逆否三种; ↔ 证两个方向.

思考题 "为什么证 ¬P → Q 就证了 P ∨ Q": 两者真值表相同. ¬P → Q 只在 ¬P 真且 Q 假, 即 P 假且 Q 假时为假, 正是 P ∨ Q 为假的唯一情形.

guide_to_proofs_on_discrete_structures · Page 2–3

Assuming Statements

AssumingHow
∀x. PInitially, do nothing. Do not introduce any variables. Later, should you find some object z, you can assume P is true for that choice of z.
∃x. PIntroduce a new variable that has property P.
¬PNegate P, then use this table to see what you're now assuming.
P ∧ QAssume both that P is true and that Q is true.
P ∨ QConsider two separate cases, one where P is true and one where Q is true.
P → QInitially, do nothing. Later, if you find that P is true, you can assume that Q is also true.
P ↔ QAssume both P → Q and Q → P, using the rules above. Or, alternatively, go by cases, one in which you assume both P and Q and one in which you assume both ¬P and ¬Q.

Important Note: One of the most common mistakes that we see around this point in CS103 is not properly distinguishing between what it means to assume the statement ∀x. P and to prove the statement ∀x. P. … Think of a formula of the form ∀x. P as being like a hammer. It says “if you find a nail, you can use this tool to hit the nail.” If I handed you a hammer and said “please hang this picture frame up on the wall,” you wouldn't start swinging the hammer around hoping that you'd hit a nail somewhere.

… if you're assuming an existential statement is true, you can immediately say something like “we know there is an x where P is true” … A good example is going from “n is even” to “there exists an integer k where n = 2k.” You basically get k for free.

假设各种结构时: ∀ 先不动, 不引入变量, 等出现具体对象 z 时再用在 z 上; ∃ 立刻引入一个具有该性质的新变量 ("n 是偶数" 白送一个 k); ∧ 两者都假设; ∨ 分情况; → 先不动, 等前件成立时再得出后件; ↔ 当作两个蕴涵, 或分 "都真" 和 "都假" 两种情况.

最常见的错误是把「假设 ∀」和「证明 ∀」混淆. 证明 ∀x. P 要引入任选的 x; 假设 ∀x. P 时不能引入 x. 比喻: ∀ 像一把锤子, 意思是「找到钉子就能敲」; 拿到锤子去挂画, 你会先找钉子, 而不是挥着锤子乱砸. 「假设 →」同理, 不要立刻写 "assume P".

对照记忆: 证明时 ∀ 是读者选、∃ 是自己找; 假设时 ∃ 白送变量、∀ 要等待时机. 恰好反过来.

证明模板: 双射与单射
Proof Template: Bijections · Injectivity

guide_to_proofs_on_discrete_structures · Page 3–4

Proof: We will prove that f is injective and surjective. First, we'll prove that f is injective. (…) Next, we'll prove that f is surjective. (…) ■

… you might come across a problem like this one: Let f : ℝ → ℝ be the function f(x) = x³ + 3x + 1. Prove that f is a bijection. … notice that we didn't repeat the definition of the function f at the top of the proof … As a great exercise, go and fill in the blank spots in the above proof!

On the other hand, you might be asked to show that an arbitrary function meeting some criteria is also a bijection. … Prove that if f : A → A is an involution, then f is a bijection. … Proof: Pick an arbitrary involution f : A → A. We will prove that f is injective and surjective. …

To prove that f is injective, you need to show that ∀x1​∈A. ∀x2​∈A. (f(x1​)=f(x2​)→x1​=x2​). … Consider some arbitrary x1​,x2​∈A where f(x1​)=f(x2​). We want to show that x1​=x2​. (…)

… f : ℝ → ℝ defined as f(x) = 42x + 137. … Proof: Consider some arbitrary real numbers x1​ and x2​ where f(x1​)=f(x2​). We want to show that x1​=x2​. To see this, note that since f(x1​)=f(x2​), we have 42x1​+137=42x2​+137. (…)

(…) Consider some arbitrary x1​,x2​∈A where f(x1​)=f(x2​). We want to show that x1​=x2​. To see this, note that since f(x1​)=f(x2​), we know that f(f(x1​))=f(f(x2​)). Then, since f is an involution, we see that x1​=x2​, as required. (…)

… there are two equivalent ways of defining what it means for a function f : A → B to be injective. … ∀x1​∈A. ∀x2​∈A. (x1​=x2​→f(x1​)=f(x2​)). … Consider some arbitrary x1​,x2​∈A where x1​=x2​. We want to show that f(x1​)=f(x2​). (…)

双射 = 单射 + 满射, 所以证明分两段. 两种情形: f 是具体给定的函数 (如 f(x) = x³ + 3x + 1), 证明里不要重抄 f 的定义; f 是任意满足某条件的函数 (如任意对合), 则要先让读者任选这样的 f, 因为命题是全称的.

单射模板直接读一阶定义: 两个 ∀ → 读者任选 x₁、x₂; 蕴涵 → 假设 f(x₁) = f(x₂), 目标 x₁ = x₂. 之后: 有具体定义就代入展开 (42x₁ + 137 = 42x₂ + 137, 两边减 137 再除以 42); 只知道性质就用性质 (对合: 两边再作用 f, 得 x₁ = f(f(x₁)) = f(f(x₂)) = x₂). 也可以用等价的逆否定义: 假设 x₁ ≠ x₂, 证 f(x₁) ≠ f(x₂). 证明里不出现量词和联结词.

留作练习的 x³ + 3x + 1: 单射, 因为 x₁ < x₂ 时 x₁³ < x₂³ 且 3x₁ < 3x₂, 所以 f 严格递增; 满射, 要对任意 b 找 a 使 a³ + 3a + 1 = b, 三次方程总有实根 (可用卡尔达诺公式写出, 或用连续函数的介值定理).

证明模板: 非单射与满射
Proof Template: Not Injective · Surjectivity

guide_to_proofs_on_discrete_structures · Page 4–6

… we can simply negate that definition to show that something is not injective. … Here's the negation: ∃x1​∈A. ∃x2​∈A. (x1​=x2​∧f(x1​)=f(x2​)).

Let x1​=__ and x2​=__. We need to show that x1​=x2​ and that f(x1​)=f(x2​). (…)

… The hard part of writing a proof like this is probably going to be coming up with what choices of objects you're going to pick in the first place rather than writing down your reasoning.

If you want to prove that f is surjective, you need to prove that the following statement is true: ∀b∈B. ∃a∈A. f(a)=b. … Pick any b ∈ B. Now, let a = __. We need to show that f(a) = b.

Proof Template Exercises — Write a proof template for showing that a function f … i. is an involution: ∀a ∈ A. f(f(a)) = a. ii. is idempotent: ∀a ∈ A. f(f(a)) = f(a). iii. has a fixed point: ∃a ∈ A. f(a) = a. iv. is doubly covered: ∀b∈B. ∃a1​∈A. ∃a2​∈A. (a1​=a2​∧f(a1​)=f(a2​)=b).

证明「不是单射」: 对定义取否定, 得到两个 ∃, 所以作者要亲自指定 x₁、x₂, 再验证它们不同但函数值相同. 难点在找出这对元素, 要画图、试例子.

满射模板: ∀b → 读者任选 b; ∃a → 作者根据 b 构造 a (难点); 最后验证 f(a) = b. 例如 f(x) = 42x + 137 时取 a = (b − 137)/42.

练习的模板: (i) 任选 a ∈ A, 要证 f(f(a)) = a. (ii) 任选 a ∈ A, 要证 f(f(a)) = f(a). (iii) 令 a = __, 要证 f(a) = a. (iv) 任选 b ∈ B, 令 a₁ = __、a₂ = __, 要证 a₁ ≠ a₂ 且 f(a₁) = f(a₂) = b. 规律都是: ∀ 读者选, ∃ 作者选, 剩下的是要验证的内容.

定义函数与写较长的证明
Defining Functions · Writing Longer Proofs

guide_to_proofs_on_discrete_structures · Page 7–9

… In all cases, you should be sure to do the following: 1. Give the domain and codomain. 2. Give a rule explaining how to evaluate the function. … Consider the function f : ℕ → ℕ defined as f(n) = n + 1.

Consider the function f : ℤ → ℤ defined as follows: f(x)={x2x3​if x<0if x≥0​

… the written proof doesn't require you to exhaustively confirm that all cases are covered, but you absolutely should do this on your own … Let h = g ∘ f. At this point, no further elaboration is necessary. … The last way you can define a function is by drawing pictures showing the domain and codomain and how the function is evaluated. … Consider the function f : A → B defined below: (picture: A has three elements ○, □, ◇; ○ maps to ☺, □ and ◇ both map to ☼.)

A lemma is a smaller proof that helps establish a larger result. The distinction between a lemma and a theorem is purely one of context. … Lemma 1: For all whagfis x, if x is gammiferous, then x is haoqi-complete. … Lemma 2: Let Q be an o'a'aa. Then Q is a syththony. … Theorem: Every ichenochen is a zichenzochen. Proof: … By Lemma 1, we know that q is haoqi-complete. By Gloomenberg's Theorem, we know that q is an o'a'aa, so by Lemma 2 we know that q is a syththony. …

定义函数时必须给出定义域、陪域和求值规则. 四种写法: 一个表达式 (f(n) = n + 1); 分段函数 (负数平方、非负数立方; 自己要检查各段覆盖了所有输入, 证明里不必写); 用已有函数组合 (h = g ∘ f, 不用再解释); 有限集合上画映射图 (图中 ○ ↦ ☺, □ 和 ◇ 都 ↦ ☼, 这个例子正好是满射但不是单射).

较长的证明用 lemma 引理拆开, 就像把长函数拆成辅助函数. 引理与定理的区别只在语境: 定理是最终结论, 引理是中间用到的小结论 (技术性细节, 或大结论的一部分). 先陈述并证明引理, 主证明里写 "By Lemma 1" 引用, 主证明就短而清楚.

离散结构证明检查清单
Discrete Structures Proofwriting Checklist

discrete_structures_checklist · Page 1

… there are a few specific points we'd like to you to check for in your proofs in addition to the general rules set out in the earlier Proofwriting Checklist.

  • Appropriately call back to first-order definitions.
  • Don't use quantifiers or connectives in your proofs.
  • Don't repeat definitions; use them instead.
  • Distinguish between assuming and proving.
  • Type-check your proofs.

写离散结构的证明时, 在前面 8 条之外再检查 5 条: 回到一阶定义; 不用量词和联结词; 使用定义而不是复述; 分清假设与证明; 对证明做类型检查. 原文 "we'd like to you to check" 多了一个 to.

回到一阶定义
Appropriately Call Back to First-Order Definitions

discrete_structures_checklist · Page 1–2

… let's suppose that you're trying to prove that some function f : A → B is surjective. … you should not start your proof off like this:

⚠ Incorrect! ⚠ Proof: Consider any x1​,x2​∈A where x1​=x2​. Since x1​=x2​, we know that (…) ■

… we're essentially writing a proof that matches the following first-order logic fragment: ∀x1​∈A. ∀x2​∈A. (x1​=x2​→(…))

… You're asked to prove that if f³ is a bijection, then f is a bijection. Here's an (incorrect!) proof of this.

⚠ Incorrect! ⚠ Proof: The function f³ is defined in terms of the function f. Therefore, properties of f³ will transmit to f. And since f³ is a bijection, this means that f must be as well. ■

… First, be wary about going off-script in the course of writing a proof. … This brings us to the second lesson here – exercise skepticism about broad claims in your proofs.

一阶定义精确告诉你要证什么, 所以开头的结构必须和定义一致. 证满射却写 "任取 x₁ ≠ x₂", 对应的是单射 (的逆否形式) 的结构, 一开始就错了. 动手之前先写清假设什么、要证什么.

另一种失败是层次太高: "f³ 由 f 定义, 所以 f³ 的性质会传给 f". 这是用一个更宽泛、没证过的说法 ("函数变换后有某性质, 原函数就有该性质") 来证一个窄命题, 而宽泛的说法其实是假的. 例如 f: ℤ → ℤ, f(x) = 2x 不是满射, 而 g(x) = ⌊x/2⌋ 也不是单射, 但 g ∘ f 是恒等函数, 是双射, 所以「组合后的性质会传回各部分」不成立. 教训: ① 要证某对象有某性质, 就逐条对照定义去证, 走别的路要格外怀疑; ② 对证明里的宽泛断言保持怀疑, 要么证明它, 要么推翻它.

不用量词与联结词, 不复述定义
Don't Use Quantifiers or Connectives · Don't Repeat Definitions

discrete_structures_checklist · Page 2–4

⚠ Incorrect! ⚠ Proof: We will prove that the function is surjective. To do so, we need to prove that ∀b ∈ B. ∃a ∈ A. f(a) = b. So consider ∀b ∈ B. We will prove that ∃a ∈ A where f(a) = b. (…) ■

Proof: We will prove that the function f is surjective. To do so, consider an arbitrary b ∈ B. We need to prove that there is some a ∈ A where f(a) = b. (…) ■

⚠ We know that x ∈ A. Since A ⊆ B, we know that every element of A is an element of B. Thus we see that x ∈ B. ⚠ … They're better off rewritten like this: Since x ∈ A and A ⊆ B, we see that x ∈ B.

⚠ Incorrect! ⚠ Proof: Let f : A → A be an involution. … pick any a1​,a2​∈A where f(a1​)=f(a2​). … We know that f is an involution, so for any a1​∈A, we know that f(f(a1​))=a1​. Similarly, for any a2​, we know that f(f(a2​))=a2​. …

… Imagine that they've picked a₁ = 137. At this point in the proof, we're now talking about “for any a₁ ∈ A.” From the perspective of the person reading the proof, this is like saying “for any 137.” It's not a meaningful statement. … just say something like this: We know that f is an involution, so f(f(a1​))=a1​.

"consider ∀b ∈ B" 既用了符号, 又只是复述满射的定义; 删掉这句, 改成 "consider an arbitrary b ∈ B" 即可. 复述定义的三种写法 (太泛、变量作用域不清、对占位符断言) 和普通检查清单里一样, 一律改成直接应用: "Since x ∈ A and A ⊆ B, we see that x ∈ B."

对合的例子: a₁ 已经是读者选定的具体值 (比如 137), 再说 "for any a₁ ∈ A" 就像说 "对任何 137", 没有意义. 直接写 "f 是对合, 所以 f(f(a₁)) = a₁". 读者知道对合的定义, 自会查证.

分清假设与证明
Distinguish Between Assuming and Proving

discrete_structures_checklist · Page 4–6

n is even when ∃k ∈ ℤ. n = 2k. If you are proving that a number n is even, then you need to find some integer k where n = 2k. If you are assuming that a number n is even, then you can introduce a new variable k such that n = 2k. … One is “go on a scavenger hunt to find the choice of k you want.” The other is “oh, how convenient! I get a new variable named k with some nice properties.”

… if you are assuming that a function f is injective, then you do not introduce any variables, and instead wait to see if you find any values y₁ and y₂ where f(y₁) = f(y₂). If so, you can then conclude that y₁ = y₂.

⚠ Incorrect! ⚠ Proof: Let f : A → A be an involution. We will prove that f is injective. Since f is an involution, for any x ∈ A, we know that f(f(x)) = x. We also know that for any x ∈ A that f(f(x)) = x. (…) ■

… This mistake – introducing a variable when assuming a universally-quantified statement – is hard to recover from. … There are a couple of indicators … 1. If you find yourself talking about how something is true “for all x,” it might indicate that you're trying to use a universally-quantified assumption before you're ready to do so. … 2. If you had the reader pick an arbitrary value and later on discover that it should have some specific, concrete value, it might mean that you've started off with a universally-quantified assumption, introduced a variable for it …

同一个定义, 假设和证明时的用法完全不同. 「n 是偶数」: 证明时要去「寻宝」找 k; 假设时白得一个 k. 「f 是单射」: 证明时引入读者任选的 x₁、x₂; 假设时不引入变量, 等出现 f(y₁) = f(y₂) 时才得出 y₁ = y₂.

从奇偶数 (大多是存在型定义) 转到函数 (大多是全称型定义) 时这点尤其重要. 错误示范在假设对合时引入了 x, 既没说明来源, 又是在复述定义, 只能删掉重来. 两个警报信号: ① 写出「对所有 x」, 可能是在过早使用全称假设; ② 让读者任选了一个值, 后来又发现它应该是某个具体值, 可能一开始就把全称假设当成了要证的全称命题.

原文 "which statements you're proving," 句子在逗号处中断, 后半句缺失.

类型检查
Type-Check Your Proofs

discrete_structures_checklist · Page 6

Let's imagine that f : A → B is a function and that x is an element of A. There's a difference between the function f (a general transformation that can be applied to elements of A) and the object f(x), which is a specific object contained in the set B. In other words:

  • f is of type “function.”
  • f(x) is of type “element of B”

This means, for example, that you could say something like “f is injective” or “f is a bijection,” but you shouldn't write something like “f(x) is injective” or “f(x) is a bijection,” since f(x) refers specifically to what you get when you plug x into f. As a note, in practice, mathematicians tend to sometimes be a lot looser with the distinction between f and f(x) …

f 是函数, f(x) 是 B 的一个元素, 类型不同. 可以说 "f 是单射", 不能说 "f(x) 是单射". 数学家平时常混用 f 和 f(x), 但 CS103 要求严格区分, 以表明你理解两者不是一回事. 这延续了集合翻译、一阶逻辑翻译里的类型检查.

归纳法指南
Guide to Induction

归纳证明模板
The Inductive Proof Template

guide_to_induction · Page 1
  1. Define some predicate P(n) that you'll prove by induction. … To make explicit what predicate that is, begin your proof by spelling out what predicate you'll be proving something about by induction.
  2. State that the proof is by induction. … If you're going to prove P(n) is true for all natural numbers, say that. If you're going to prove that P(n) is true for all even natural numbers greater than five, make that clear.
  3. State and prove your base case. … We recommend explicitly writing out what P(0) actually states before you try to prove it. … “We will prove P(0), which states that …”
  4. State and prove the inductive step. … We recommend specifically writing out both what the assumption P(k) means and what you're going to prove when you show P(k + 1).
  5. Conclude the proof. This usually isn't too much – you can just say something like “completing the induction” and add the little boxy ■ symbol.

初学阶段推荐的五步模板: ① 定义要归纳证明的谓词 P(n); ② 宣布用归纳法, 并说明对哪些数证明 (全体自然数, 还是大于 5 的偶数等); ③ 写出并证明基础情形, 先写明 P(0) 说的是什么; ④ 写出并证明归纳步, 同时写明假设 P(k) 的内容和要证的 P(k + 1) 的内容; ⑤ 收尾 "completing the induction" ■. 对应 CS103 12、13.

P(n) 是什么
A Guide to P(n)

guide_to_induction · Page 1–2

Formally speaking, induction works in the following way. Given some predicate P(n), an inductive proof proves P(0) is true as a base case; proves that if P(k) is true, then P(k + 1) must be true as well; and concludes that P(n) is true for any natural number n.

As an example, suppose that you want to prove this result from Problem Set Five: For any n ∈ ℕ, an​ is both square and triangular. … One possible choice of P(n) could be this one: P(n) is the statement “an​ is both square and triangular.” … For example, P(4) is the statement a4​ is both square and triangular.

… if we can prove that P(n) is true for all choices of natural number n, we'll have a proof of our overall statement.

As a quick note: the notation P(n) might seem confusing – it looks like it's some function of the number n. However, P(n) isn't a mathematical quantity. Instead, it's a predicate – a logical assertion saying something about the number n.

归纳法的形式: 证 P(0), 证 "P(k) → P(k + 1)", 得出对所有自然数 n 有 P(n). 选 P(n) 的标准: 「P(n) 对所有 n 成立」展开后正好是要证的定理. 例如要证 "对所有 n, aₙ 既是平方数又是三角数", 就取 P(n) = "aₙ 既是平方数又是三角数"; 代入具体的 n 得到一个可真可假的命题, 如 P(4) 说 a₄ 既是平方数又是三角数. P(n) 是谓词 (关于 n 的断言), 不是数, 不能当成数来运算.

归纳的方向
Directionality in Induction

guide_to_induction · Page 2–3

(Incorrect!) Proof: Let P(n) be the statement “the sum of the first n powers of two is 2n−1.” … For the inductive step, assume that P(k) is true for some arbitrary k ∈ ℕ, meaning that 20+21+⋯+2k−1=2k−1. We will prove that P(k + 1) is true, meaning that the sum of the first k + 1 powers of two is 2k+1−1. To see this, note that

20+⋯+2k−1+2k20+⋯+2k−1+2k20+⋯+2k−1+2k20+⋯+2k−1​=2k+1−1=2(2k)−1=2k+2k−1=2k−1​

We've arrived at our inductive hypothesis, which we know is true. Therefore, P(k + 1) is true, completing the induction. ■

… if the proof says it's going to prove something, why is it stating it as if it were a mathematical fact? … It begins by assuming that the sum of the first k + 1 powers of two is 2k+1−1, then proceeds from there to prove that under this assumption, the sum of the first k powers of two is 2k−1. In other words, the proof has gone backwards; it assumed P(k + 1) is true and used that to prove P(k) is true.

归纳步要证的是 "P(k) → P(k + 1)", 很容易不小心写反. 错误示范一开头就把要证的等式当作已知写出来, 然后两边化简, 最后得到归纳假设, 宣布证完. 每一步代数都对, 但证的方向是 "P(k + 1) → P(k)", 结论是错的. 判断信号: 证明说「要证 X」, 紧接着却把 X 当事实写出来.

正确写法是从左边出发写等式链: 20+⋯+2k−1+2k=(2k−1)+2k=2k+1−1, 第一步用归纳假设.

选择基础情形
Choosing and Proving Base Cases

guide_to_induction · Page 3–4

There are four main reasons we chose to use these base cases. First, we chose our base cases to make sure that the theorems we proved were true for every natural number n, not just some of them. …

Second, we chose these extremely simple base cases because they're as simplified as they can possibly be. … Philosophically, it's the job of the inductive step to try to simplify, and it's the job of the base case to show that when no more simplification is possible, the result must be true. … After all, you can't make fewer than 0 weighings, or sum up fewer than 0 numbers.

Third, choosing the absolute simplest possible base case forces you to think about the extreme cases of the result. … For example, it is not true that a square can be subdivided into 0 squares.

Finally, in some cases, choosing the absolutely simplest possible base case can actually make your proof shorter and simpler. … if you find yourself using similar reasoning in your base case and your inductive step, chances are you can make your base case even simpler!

二的幂之和取 n = 0 (零个数的和), 假币问题取零次称量, 理由有四: ① 定理要对所有自然数成立, 包括 0, 从 1 开始会漏掉一个情况; ② 最简单: 归纳步负责化简, 基础情形负责「无法再化简时结论成立」, 不可能少于零次称量、少于零个数相加; ③ 逼你思考极端情形, 有时会发现结论在边界不成立 (正方形不能分成 0 个正方形), 有时会发现直觉没想到的成立情形; ④ 往往更短: 如果基础情形取「三枚硬币称一次」, 就得在基础情形里重复归纳步的推理. 经验: 基础情形和归纳步的推理相似, 说明基础情形还能更简单.

普通归纳还是强归纳
Induction or Complete Induction?

guide_to_induction · Page 4–5

… Suppose that as part of your inductive step, you're trying to prove that the result is true for k + 1. If you can always prove this purely by assuming that the result is true for k, then you can just use normal induction. On the other hand, if you need to assume that the result is true for some number between 0 and k, inclusive, but you're not sure in advance which of those numbers it's going to be, you should use complete induction …

… we proved that a 1 × n chocolate bar can be eaten in 2n−1 ways for any n ≥ 1. … The size of the chocolate bar that remains after the first bite is made could be any number from 0 to k, inclusive, depending on whether we break of 1, 2, 3, …, or k + 1 pieces.

  • If you can determine in advance the size of the smaller problem, use standard induction.
  • If you can't determine the size in advance, use complete induction.

… Technically speaking, you never need to use standard induction. … From a stylistic perspective, though, it's not considered good form to use complete induction unless you actually need those extra assumptions.

归纳步里要用「更小的情形」时, 若总是恰好用 k, 就用普通归纳; 若可能用到 0 到 k 之间的任何一个, 事先不知道是哪个, 就用 complete induction 强归纳. 巧克力例子: 1 × (k + 1) 的巧克力第一口可以掰下 1 到 k + 1 块, 剩下 0 到 k 块都有可能, 所以需要强归纳.

启发规则: 能事先确定子问题大小就用普通归纳, 否则用强归纳. 强归纳在技术上包含普通归纳, 但风格上只在确实需要额外假设时才用, 归纳方式应反映论证结构. 原文 "break of" 应为 "break off".

向上、向下, 还是都不是
Up, Down, or Neither?

guide_to_induction · Page 5–6

… you're asked to prove, by induction, that any group of n emcees can be housed in at most seven hotels. … choose P(n) as the statement “any group of n emcees, each of whom has gifts for at most three others, can be housed in seven hotels.”

⚠ Incorrect ⚠ Line of Reasoning: … To do so, begin by taking any group M of k emcees, each of whom has gifts for at most three others. Add in another emcee e to form a group M′ of k + 1 emcees …

… we are assuming a universally-quantified statement and proving a universally-quantified statement. … to assume a universally-quantified statement, you initially do nothing. … To prove a universally-quantified statement, we make an arbitrary choice of object, then try to prove it has some property. In this case, that means picking an arbitrary group of k + 1 emcees, then trying to find a way to house those emcees. … our approach will probably be something to the effect of finding a emcee to remove from our bigger group, rather than finding a emcee to add to a smaller group.

To summarize – before you write out a proof by induction, write out explicitly what the inductive step will be. … When it doubt, write it out!

常见错误: P(n) = "任何 n 个主持人 (每人最多给三个人送礼) 都能住进七家酒店". 归纳步若写成「取 k 个人, 再加一个人得到 k + 1 个人」, 就只证明了某些能由 k 人组加一人得到的 k + 1 人组, 并没有处理任意的 k + 1 人组. 正确思路: 归纳步是「假设全称 → 证全称」, 假设时等待, 证明时任选一个 k + 1 人组, 然后从中去掉一人, 对剩下的 k 人用归纳假设, 再把去掉的人安排回去.

总结: 先把归纳步的蕴涵完整写出来, 按证明蕴涵的一般规则处理. 结果可能是从 k + 1 缩到 k, 可能是从 k 长到 k + 1, 也可能都不是. 原文 "presents problem problem" 多了一个 problem, "When it doubt" 应为 "When in doubt".

练习
Exercises

guide_to_induction · Page 6–7
  1. … For all natural numbers n, the sum of the first n natural numbers is 2n(n−1)​. Give a choice of P(n) …
  2. … For all odd natural numbers n, there is a tournament with n players where every player is a champion. Give a choice of P(n) …
  3. Prove that for every natural number n ≥ 1, we have 1⋅21​+2⋅31​+⋯+n(n+1)1​=n+1n​.
  4. a0​=1, a1​=3, a2​=7, an+3​=an​+an+1​. … Prove that a0​+a1​+⋯+an​=an+5​−10 for all n ∈ ℕ.
  5. (Contract rummy: rounds need 6, 7, 8, …, 12 cards built from sets of three and sequences of four.) Prove, by induction, that any natural number greater than or equal to six can be written as 3m + 4n for some natural numbers m and n.
  6. Vn​={Vk​∣k∈N∧k<n}. … the magnitude of a set S, denoted M(S), to be one plus the sum of the magnitudes of all its elements. (The magnitude of a non-set is defined to be zero.) Prove by complete induction that M(Vn​)=2n for all n ∈ ℕ.
  7. … Prove … for every graph G, if every node of G has degree c or less, then there exists a (c + 1)-vertex-coloring of G. As a hint, use induction on the number of nodes in G.
  8. … Prove by induction that for all natural numbers n, there exists a coloring of the edges of K2n​ using n colors that does not have any monochrome triangles.

答案要点:

  1. P(n): "前 n 个自然数 (0 到 n − 1) 之和是 n(n − 1)/2". 不要写成 "对任意 n …" (见下一节的作用域规则).
  2. 不能直接对奇数 n 归纳. 可取 P(n): "存在一个 2n + 1 人的锦标赛, 其中每个人都是冠军", 对所有自然数 n 证明.
  3. n = 1: 1/2 = 1/2. 归纳步: 左边加上 1/((k + 1)(k + 2)), 得 k/(k + 1) + 1/((k + 1)(k + 2)) = (k² + 2k + 1)/((k + 1)(k + 2)) = (k + 1)/(k + 2).
  4. 数列为 1, 3, 7, 4, 10, 11, 14, 21, 25, 35, …; n = 0: a₅ − 10 = 11 − 10 = 1 = a₀. 归纳步: 前 k + 2 项之和 = (aₖ₊₅ − 10) + aₖ₊₁, 只需说明 aₖ₊₆ = aₖ₊₅ + aₖ₊₁. 由递推, aₖ₊₆ − aₖ₊₅ = (aₖ₊₃ + aₖ₊₄) − (aₖ₊₂ + aₖ₊₃) = aₖ₊₄ − aₖ₊₂ = aₖ₊₁. 用 Python 核对了 n < 20 时等式成立.
  5. 三个基础情形 6 = 3·2, 7 = 3·1 + 4·1, 8 = 4·2; 归纳步每次加 3 (m 加 1). 这正是下一节说的「步长为 3 就需要三个基础情形」.
  6. V₀ = ∅, M(V₀) = 1 = 2⁰. 强归纳: M(Vₙ) = 1 + Σₖ₍₌₀₎ⁿ⁻¹ M(Vₖ) = 1 + (2⁰ + … + 2ⁿ⁻¹) = 2ⁿ.
  7. 对节点数归纳: 去掉一个节点 v, 剩下的图最大度仍 ≤ c, 由归纳假设可 (c + 1) 着色; v 至多 c 个邻居, 至少剩一种颜色可给 v. 这里是「从大缩小」, 因为 P(n) 是全称的.
  8. n = 0: K₁ 没有边. 归纳步: 把两个用 k 种颜色着好的 K2k​ 拼起来, 两半之间的所有边涂第 k + 1 种新颜色. 跨两半的三角形必有两条跨边和一条内部边, 颜色不全同; 不跨的三角形由归纳假设不单色. 这里是「从小长大」, 因为 P(n) 是存在型的.

归纳证明检查清单
Induction Proofwriting Checklist

induction_checklist · Page 1–2
  • Make P(n) a predicate, not a number or function.
  • Watch your variable scoping in P(n).
  • “Build up” if P(n) is existentially-quantified; “build down” if it's universally-quantified.
  • Choose the simplest base cases possible, and avoid redundant base cases.

… if you want to prove that an​=2n for every n ∈ ℕ, you should not define P(n) like this: ⚠ P(n)=2n ⚠ … The statement “2⁰ is true” isn't mathematically meaningful …

⚠ P(n) is “for any n ∈ ℕ, we have an​=2n.” ⚠ … consider the following piece of C++/Java-esque code:

void doSomething(int n) {
    for (int n = 0; n < 137; n++) {
        // ... do something with n ...
    }
}

Treat the argument to the predicate P like an argument to a function. The caller specifies it, and you shouldn't say something like “for any n” or “for some n” inside of the definition of P(n). (Though it is fine to talk about something like “for any group of n people” …)

四条检查. ① P(n) 必须是谓词: 归纳原理里的 P(0) 和 "P(k) → P(k + 1)" 只有在 P 取真值时才有意义. 写成 "P(n) = 2ⁿ" 是数不是命题, 应写 P(n): "aₙ = 2ⁿ".

② P(n) 内部不要再量化 n: "P(n) 是 '对任意 n ∈ ℕ, aₙ = 2ⁿ'" 里有两个 n, 就像函数参数 n 又在 for 循环里重新声明一个 n. 「对所有 n」由归纳法从外部提供; P(n) 里可以说「任意 n 个人组成的组」, 那是在量化人群, 不是重定义 n.

induction_checklist · Page 2–4

… In the proof that a square can be subdivided into smaller squares, the inductive step starts off with a subdivision of the square into k squares, then uses that to form a subdivision of the square into k + 3 squares. In the proof about counterfeit coins, the inductive step starts with a group of 3k+1 coins, then breaks it apart into three groups of 3k coins each.

P(n) is “∃S. (S is a subdivision of a square ∧ S has n squares)”
P(n) is “∀C. (C is a group of 3ⁿ coins → C's counterfeit can be found in n weighings)”

… If it's existentially-quantified, we start with something smaller and then try to grow it. If it's universally-quantified, we start with something larger and shrink it down.

… what if it's neither of these? … P(n) is the statement “the sum of the first n powers of two is 2n−1.” … Begin by writing out the first k + 1 powers of two … Use our inductive hypothesis … Invoke the Great Power of Algebra to simplify this to 2k+1−1. … A different route would be … Begin with the inductive hypothesis … Add 2k to both sides … This would also be perfectly fine, since at no point do we assume some equality we don't know to be true.

③ 方向由 P(n) 最外层的量词决定:

  • 存在型 (正方形能分成 n 个正方形): 假设前件 = 手上已有一个大小为 k 的具体对象; 要证存在大小 k + 1 (或 k + 3) 的对象, 自然是把手上的对象扩大. 「向上建」.
  • 全称型 (任意 3ⁿ 枚硬币都能在 n 次称量内找到假币): 假设前件是一把锤子, 不给对象; 要证全称, 先任选一个大小 k + 1 的对象, 再把它缩小成能用假设的大小 k. 「向下建」.
  • 都不是 (二的幂求和等式): 写出蕴涵, 按一般规则处理. 从左边出发写等式链, 或从归纳假设出发两边同加 2ᵏ, 都可以, 只要不把未证的等式当已知.

「向上」「向下」只是简记, 根本规则仍是: 假设前件, 证明后件. 原文有几处笔误: "then predicate P is" 应为 "the predicate", "it has to some some key property" 应为 "it has to have some key property", "the only we we could" 应为 "the only way we could".

induction_checklist · Page 4–5
  1. Are all the numbers you need to have covered covered? … if you're going to prove that something is true for all natural numbers, you'll need to ensure that you've covered the zero case …
  2. Have you thought through degenerate cases? Often times, the base case of an inductive proof involves an extreme sort of edge case (a set of no elements, an implication that's vacuously true, a sum of no numbers, a graph with no nodes, etc.)
  3. Does the logic in your inductive step apply to your base case? … Is the reasoning there just a special case of the reasoning in your inductive step? If so, that might indicate that you haven't actually picked the simplest possible base case …
  4. If you have multiple base cases, are they truly necessary? Some proofs by induction really do need multiple base cases, such as the square subdivision problem from lecture (where we need one base case for each remainder modulo three). …

"Everything should be as simple as possible, but no simpler."

… Our proof about square subdivisions needed three base cases because we were taking steps of size three and needed to cover all the possible remainders modulo three. If we removed any of the proofs of P(6), P(7), or P(8), then we wouldn't cover all natural numbers n ≥ 6. However, adding in more base cases (say, P(9), P(10), or P(11)) wouldn't accomplish anything new.

④ 基础情形要最简单, 也不要多余. 四个自查问题: 要覆盖的数都覆盖了吗 (证全体自然数却从 1 开始, 多半是逻辑错误); 想过退化情形吗 (空集、空真蕴涵、零个数之和、没有节点的图); 基础情形的推理是不是归纳步的特例 (是的话还能更简单); 多个基础情形真的都必要吗. 大多数证明只需一个基础情形; 正方形分割的步长是 3, 需要 6、7、8 三个, 分别覆盖模 3 的三个余数, 再加 9、10、11 只会增加出错的地方. 爱因斯坦 (传) 的话: 尽可能简单, 但不能过于简单.

子集构造指南
Guide to the Subset Construction

guide_to_the_subset_construction · Page 1

This animated guide explains how the subset construction works with ε-transitions and Σ-transitions. Guide to the Subset Construction

入口页: 一份动画指南, 演示带 ε 转移和 Σ 转移 (读任意字符都走的转移) 时子集构造怎么做. 内容见 CS103 15.

子集构造的步骤复习: ① DFA 的起始状态是 NFA 起始状态的 ε 闭包 (从它出发只走 ε 转移能到的所有状态); ② 对 DFA 的每个状态 (一个 NFA 状态集合 S) 和每个字符 x, 先收集 S 中每个状态读 x 能到的状态 (Σ 转移对每个字符都算), 再取 ε 闭包, 得到新状态; ③ 含有 NFA 接受状态的集合都是 DFA 的接受状态; ④ 空集是一个合法的 DFA 状态 (陷阱状态), 不能省略. 只需要生成从起始状态可达的集合, 不必列出全部 2ⁿ 个.

正则表达式指南
Guide to Regular Expressions

guide_to_regexes · Page 1

Regular expressions are an amazingly powerful tool for describing collections of strings. However, they can take some time to get used to and represent a totally different problem-solving strategy than the techniques for designing automata.

  • Union represents choice. Intuitively, you can think of a regex of the form A ∪ B as saying "something matching pattern A or something matching pattern B."
  • Concatenation represents sequencing. You can think of a regex of the form AB as meaning "match pattern A, then match pattern B."
  • Kleene stars represent iteration. You can think of a regex of the form R⋆ as saying "as many copies of R as you'd like."

设计正则表达式和设计自动机是两种不同的解题思路. 三种组合方式各有直观含义: 并 ∪ 表示选择, 连接表示先后顺序, 克林星号表示重复任意多次. 学写正则就是熟练运用这三样工具. 对应 CS103 17.

原文排版问题: 第三条里的 R⋆ 没有被网页渲染, PDF 中显示为 LaTeX 源码 "R⋆".

先写具体测试串
Write Out Concrete Test Cases

guide_to_regexes · Page 1–2

Before you even start writing your regex, take a few minutes to write out two groups of strings: one group of strings that does meet the criteria, and one group that doesn't. The positive examples will help you hypothesize patterns that you can use as the basis for your regex. The negative examples will help you test those hypothesized patterns.

L={w∈{a,b}⋆∣w begins and ends with the same letter}

Strings in LStrings Not in L
abbaaabb

  • The empty string isn't in the language, so every string in L has to have length one or more.
  • Strings consisting of just a single character are in L. …
  • If the string has length two or more, then what comes between the first and last characters of the string are irrelevant.

动笔之前, 先写两组串: 属于语言的 (用来猜模式) 和不属于的 (用来检验猜想); 两组以后都是测试用例. 要尽量多样: 很短的和中等长度的、单一字符重复的和混合的、有规律的和随机的. 尤其要写出长度 0、1、2 的串, 边界情况最容易漏.

例子: 首尾字母相同的串. 从表中观察到: 空串不在 L 中; 单个字符的串都在 L 中 (首字符就是尾字符); 长度 ≥ 2 时中间是什么无所谓. 这些从定义也能推出, 但有具体的串摆在眼前就容易得多.

用并表示不同情况
Encode Distinct Choices Using Unions

guide_to_regexes · Page 2–3
  1. Strings that are one letter long.
  2. Strings that begin with an a and end with a second copy of a.
  3. Strings that begin with a b and end with a second copy of b.

… For strings of length one … a more compact way to do this would be to just use Σ, which is a regex meaning "any individual character." For strings that begin with a and end with a second copy of a, we can write aΣ⋆a. This says "match an a, then anything (that's what Σ⋆ means), then anothe a). … By simplying unioning all these together, we get a regex that covers all of the needed cases:

Σ∪aΣ⋆a∪bΣ⋆b

You might be wondering whether there's a way to combine those last two cases together … Alas, the answer is "no, there's no way to combine those." Regexes don't have a notion of "memory" in the sense of "remember the first character you read." (That being said, some regex libraries widely used in practice do have a notion of backreferences …)

把 L 中的串分成三类互不相关的情况: 长度 1; a 开头 a 结尾; b 开头 b 结尾. 每类都比原语言简单, 分别写成 Σ、aΣ⋆a、bΣ⋆b, 再用 ∪ 并起来. 后两类不能合并: 正则表达式没有「记住第一个字符」的能力. 实际中有些正则库支持反向引用 (如 (.).*\1), 但那已超出正则语言, 是理论与实践的差别. 写好后用前面的两组串测试 (我们用 Python 对长度 ≤ 6 的所有串核对过这个表达式).

原文笔误: "anothe a" 应为 "another a", "simplying" 应为 "simply".

把长串分块
Split Larger Strings Into Blocks

guide_to_regexes · Page 3

L={w∈{a,b,c}⋆∣w does not contain abc as a substring}

… Regexes unfortunately don't have a nice way of saying "everything except for the following." … we have to convert our description from "strings that don't do X" to "strings that do do Y."

Strings in LStrings Not in L
aaaaaabc

  • Any string that doesn't use all three of a, b, and c is in L.
  • It's always fine for a b to have an a or a b after it.
  • It's always fine for an a to have an a or a c after it.
  • The letter c can be followed by anything.
  • It's only okay for an a to have a b after it if that b doesn't have a c after it.

第二个例子: 不含子串 abc 的串. 正则没有「除了……」的写法, 只能把「不做 X」转成「做 Y」. 观察: 只用到两种字母的串都在 L 中; b 后面可以接 a 或 b; a 后面可以接 a 或 c; c 后面接什么都行; a 后面接 b 时, 那个 b 后面不能接 c.

这些是同时成立的多个约束, 不能用并来组合 (正则也没有交). 但它们都是「某字母后面能接什么」, 提示我们只需盯住每个 a 附近发生的事.

原文错误: 测试表有两个串放错了栏. "acbbacbcacabcba" 列在 "Strings in L", 但它含有 abc (倒数第 6 到第 4 个字符 …cabcba); "acbbacacbbcaacb" 列在 "Strings Not in L", 但它不含 abc. 用 Python 检查了两栏全部 22 个串, 只有这两个错. 后文说用这些测试串检验最终表达式全部通过, 实际上最终表达式对这两个串给出的是正确答案, 与表中的分栏相反.

Given any string w that's in L, imagine splitting w apart into a bunch of smaller blocks of characters based on the positions of the letter a. … {something} a {something} a … a {something} a {something}

​c(b∪c)⋆∪b∪bb(b∪c)⋆∪ε=(bb∪c)(b∪c)⋆∪b∪ε​

按 a 的位置把串切成块: {something} a {something} a … a {something}, 其中 {something} 只含 b 和 c. 两步走: 先写出「块与 a 交替」的总体结构, 再写出块本身.

交替结构: {something}(a{something})⋆, 首尾都是块 (可以为空), 正好对应第一个 a 之前和最后一个 a 之后的部分.

块能是什么: 列出「能跟在 a 后面」和「不能」的 b/c 串. 规律: 以 c 开头的都行, 单个 b 行, 以 bb 开头的都行, 空串行; 不行的都以 bc 开头. 四种情况互不重叠, 可以并起来; c 开头和 bb 开头可以合并成 (bb∪c)(b∪c)⋆.

guide_to_regexes · Page 5–6

((bb∪c)(b∪c)⋆∪b∪ε)(a((bb∪c)(b∪c)⋆∪b∪ε))⋆

If we run all of those strings through, we will find that they all do the right thing… with two exceptions. The string bc is in L, but it does not match this regex, and the same is true for bcacb. …

… we want {something} to represent "something that can follow an a," and bc can't follow an a. But wait a minute - look at the string bcacb. Here, the bc doesn't follow an a, because it's at the start of the string … A better way to split the string apart would be to write it like this: {before first a} a {something} a … a {something}

… any string appearing before the first a must consist purely of b's and c's … And beyond that, there really aren't any constraints. … we can do that with (b∪c)⋆.

(b∪c)⋆(a((bb∪c)(b∪c)⋆∪b∪ε))⋆

… In CS103, you're lucky because we have a theoretically perfect autograder … But in practice, you'd want to make sure to really, really thoroughly test your regex before declaring victory.

第一版把开头的块也当成「跟在 a 后面的块」, 于是 bc、bcacb 匹配失败: 它们开头的 bc 前面没有 a, 本来是合法的. 这是很常见的错误: 第一个 a 之前的部分和 a 之后的部分规则不同. 改成 {第一个 a 之前} a {something} a … a {something}, 前缀没有任何限制 (还没出现 a, 不可能形成 abc), 用 (b∪c)⋆.

最终表达式通过全部测试串. 我们用 Python 对 {a, b, c} 上长度 ≤ 8 的所有 9841 个串逐一比对, 结果与「不含 abc」完全一致. 课程有理论上完美的自动评分器 (把正则转成自动机后比较等价性); 实际工作中则要非常彻底地测试, 很多线上 bug 就出在写错的正则上.

原文笔误: "possibilites" 应为 "possibilities", "early one" 应为 "early on", "if there we an a there" 应为 "if there were an a there", "we haven't see any a's" 应为 "seen".

Exercises

guide_to_regexes · Page 6–7
  1. L={w∈{a,b}⋆∣w consists of either an even number of a's or an odd number of b's }. For example, aa ∈ L and bbb ∈ L, but a ∉ L, bbbb ∉ L, and aba ∉ L.
  2. L={w∈{a,b}⋆∣w=ab}.
  3. L={w∈{a,b,c}⋆∣∣w∣≥1 and the last character of w appears nowhere else in w }.
  4. L={w∈{a,b}⋆∣w does not contain aa or bb as substrings }.
  5. L={w∈{a,b}⋆∣w has an even number of copies of the substring ab }.
  6. Let Σ = { □/□, □/■, ■/□, ■/■ }. You can think of each character in Σ as a vertical 2 × 1 domino where each square in the domino is either black or white. … L = { w ∈ Σ* | w is a 2D grid with a white path from its upper-left corner to its bottom-right corner }. Here, we'll consider a path to be a series of steps moving up, down, left, or right. … The string ε is not in L because it has no top-left or bottom-right corner. … (□■ over ■□) would not be in L because we cannot move diagonally.

参考答案 (原文答案折叠, 以下每一条都用 Python 对短串穷举核对过):

  1. b⋆(ab⋆ab⋆)⋆∪a⋆ba⋆(ba⋆ba⋆)⋆: 前一半是偶数个 a, 后一半是奇数个 b.
  2. ε∪Σ∪aa∪bΣ∪ΣΣΣΣ⋆: 按长度分情况, 长度 2 时只排除 ab.
  3. (b∪c)⋆a∪(a∪c)⋆b∪(a∪b)⋆c: 按最后一个字符分三种情况.
  4. (ε∪b)(ab)⋆(ε∪a): 不含 aa、bb 就是 a、b 交替.
  5. b⋆(a+b+a+b+)⋆a⋆: 每出现一次 ab 就是一次「a 块 → b 块」的切换, 把切换两两配对.
  6. 记 u = 上下都白, t = 上白下黑, d = 上黑下白. 追踪当前列可到达的格子 (只有上、只有下、上下都可): 答案 t⋆u(t⋆u∪d⋆u)⋆d⋆. 第一列上格必须白; 只有经过全白的 u 列才能换行; 最后要能到达右下角.

状态消除指南
Guide to State Elimination

guide_to_state_elimination · Page 1

The state elimination algorithm transforms a DFA or NFA into regular expression. This is a big deal in Theoryland, as it shows that there's nothing you can do with DFA or NFA that you can't do with a regex. In practice, it's a useful tool to keep in your toolkit when designing regexes. While it probably shouldn't be your first line of attack when crafting regular expressions …, every now and then the state elimination algorithm ends up being one of the easiest ways to write a regex for a language.

Example: Addition Parity — Σ = {a, +, ≡}: L={am+an≡ap∣m,n,p∈N∧m+n≡2​p}. So, for example, we have aaa + aaa ≡ aaaaaa ∈ L … We also have aa + aaaa ≡ aa ∈ L … Note that + ≡ is also in the language (zero a's in each group), as are a+ ≡ a and +a ≡ a.

Since all that matters to the language is the parity (evenness/oddness) of the counts of the a's, the automaton consists of two parallel rows of states. … Every time we see an a in the top (even) set of states, we move to the bottom (odd) set of states and vice-versa.

状态消除算法把 DFA 或 NFA 转成正则表达式, 从而证明正则表达式和自动机能力相同 (见 CS103 17). 设计正则时它不是首选, 但有时是最省事的办法.

例子: 串的形式是 a 组 + a 组 ≡ a 组, 要求前两组 a 的个数之和与第三组奇偶相同. 等价于 a 的总数为偶数. 所以 NFA 只需追踪「在第几组」和「目前 a 的总数的奇偶」: 上排偶、下排奇, 每读一个 a 上下切换. 最后在第三组且总数为偶 (q2) 时接受.

guide_to_state_elimination · Page 1–2

Step One: Add in a new start state qs​ with a ε transition to the old start state. Add in a new accepting state qf​ and add ε transitions from each old accepting state to qf​. Finally, make only qf​ the accepting state.

Step Two: Eliminate all states from the NFA other than qs​ and qf​. To eliminate a state qgone​, do the following:

  1. Find all pairs of states (qin​,qout​) where qin​ has a transition to qgone​, where qgone​ has a transition to qout​, and where neither qin​ or qout​ is qgone​.
  2. For each pair (qin​,qout​), add a transition directly from qin​ to qout​. Label that transition with a regex simulating the effect of transitioning from qin​ to qgone​, following any self-loops on qgone​, then transitioning to qout​.
  3. Remove qgone​ from the automaton.
  4. Consolidate parallel transitions.
  5. (Optional) Simplify any complex regexes that arise in the process.

There is no requirement about which state we eliminate first or the order in which we eliminate the states. Any choice will work. However, some choices may work much, much better than others.

When eliminating state qgone​ and adding a transition from qin​ to qout​, where qgone​ has no self-loops, … The resulting regex on the transition from qin​ to qout​ is (Rin​)(Rout​) … where qgone​ has a self-loop … (Rin​)(Rstay​)⋆(Rout​), where the parentheses may be omitted if they don't change the meaning of the resulting regex.

Step Three: The final automaton now just has qs​ and qf​. … If there is no transition from qs​ to qf​, the final regex is ∅. Otherwise, the final regex is the label on the transition from qs​ to qf​.

算法三步:

  1. 加一个新起始状态 q_s (ε 指向旧起始状态) 和一个新的唯一接受状态 q_f (旧接受状态都 ε 指向它). 目的是最后只剩 q_s → q_f 一条边, 边上的标签就是答案.
  2. 逐个消去其他状态. 消去 q_gone 时, 对每一对「从 q_in 进、到 q_out 出」的状态, 加一条直连边, 标签是 Rin​Rout​; 若 q_gone 有自环 Rstay​, 则是 Rin​Rstay⋆​Rout​ (进来、绕任意圈、出去). q_in 和 q_out 可以是同一个状态, 此时得到自环. 然后删掉 q_gone, 把同一对状态之间的平行边用 ∪ 合并.
  3. 若 q_s 到 q_f 没有边, 答案是 ∅; 否则就是那条边的标签.

消去顺序任意, 结果都正确, 但不同顺序得到的表达式繁简差别很大.

guide_to_state_elimination · Page 2–6
EliminateInOutRegex
q3​q0​q4​a+
q0​q0​aa
q5​q4​q2​≡ a
q2​q2​aa
q4​q0​q2​a+ ≡ a
q0​q1​a + a
q1​q2​a ≡ a
q1​q1​aa
q1​q0​q2​(+∪a+a)(aa)⋆(≡∪ a≡a)

… (It's a slightly unfortunate choice of alphabet that we have + in this regex meaning "the character +" rather than "the Kleene plus operation." …)

… so our final regex ends up being (aa)⋆((+∪a+a)(aa)⋆(≡∪ a≡a)∪a+≡a)(aa)⋆

It's interesting to see how the groups are built up. All of them are built up two a's at a time. The cases where one group is odd is handled by placing an a on both sides of one of the separator symbols. When I first read this I was mystified by why there needed to be an a+ ≡ a case. … as a hint, how does the regex handle the case where the first and last group have an odd number of a's while the middle group has an even number of a's?

消去顺序 q3、q5、q4、q1, 然后 q2、q0. 每一步都按「进来 · 绕圈 · 出去」拼标签: 消去 q3 时, q0 →a→ q3 →+→ q4 得 a+, q0 →a→ q3 →a→ q0 得自环 aa; 消去 q4 后 q0 到 q2 和 q1 到 q2 出现平行边, 用 ∪ 合并; 消去带自环 aa 的 q1 时, 得到 (+∪a+a)(aa)⋆(≡∪ a≡a). 最后消去 q2 (自环 aa) 和 q0 (自环 aa), 丢掉连接上的 ε. 这里的 + 是字符加号, 不是克林加号.

读懂结果: 每组 a 都是两个两个地生成 ((aa)*); 某组为奇数时, 在分隔符两边各放一个 a 来实现 (a+a 让第一、二组都多一个, a≡a 让第二、三组都多一个). 奇 + 偶 ≡ 奇 且中间组为 0 时, 无法用 a+a 或 a≡a 凑出 (它们会让中间组至少有一个 a), 所以需要单独的 a+≡a 分支; 中间组是正偶数时, 由 a+a 和 a≡a 各贡献一个 a 得到. 我们用 Python 对长度 ≤ 9 的所有串核对了最终表达式, 与语言定义完全一致.

原文笔误: "which corresponding to" 应为 "which correspond to"; 练习里 "acccepts" 多了一个 c, "a much simple regex" 应为 "simpler".

guide_to_state_elimination · Page 6–7

Exercises

  1. Here is a DFA that acccepts all strings that contain aa as a substring: … Perform the state-elimination algorithm on this DFA, removing the states in the order q2​,q1​,q0​. What is the resulting regular expression?
  2. Perform state elimination on the same automaton as in part (i), but this time using the order q0​, then q1​, and then q2​. What regex do you get back now? This shows that the order in which states are eliminated can influence the form of the final regex.
  3. Write a much simple regex for the language of strings that contain aa as a substring than you obtained through either parts (i) or (ii) of these exercises. This shows that while state elimination is guaranteed to always convert a DFA or NFA into a regular expression, the regex you get back might not be the nicest or simplest.

答案 (三个表达式都用 Python 对长度 ≤ 10 的串核对过):

  1. 消 q2: q1 → q_f 得 aΣ⋆. 消 q1: q0 自环 ab, q0 → q_f 得 aaΣ⋆; 合并 q0 的两个自环为 b ∪ ab. 消 q0: (b∪ab)⋆aaΣ⋆.
  2. 消 q0 (自环 b): q_s → q1 得 b⋆a, q1 自环 bb⋆a. 消 q1: q_s → q2 得 b⋆a(bb⋆a)⋆a. 消 q2 (自环 Σ): b⋆a(bb⋆a)⋆aΣ⋆.
  3. Σ⋆aaΣ⋆.

Myhill-Nerode 定理指南
Guide to the Myhill-Nerode Theorem

guide_to_myhill_nerode · Page 1–2

… a nonregular language is one where you can't do any of the above. You can't build a DFA for it, or design an NFA for it, or write a regex for it.

Suppose you have a language L over some alphabet Σ. Two strings x and y are called distinguishable relative to L when there is a string w such that exactly one of xw and yw is in L.

… Consider the language L={w∈{a,b}⋆∣∣w∣=4}. … We want to show that the strings aba and bb are distinguishable relative to L. … In the example on the left, we end up with abaa (length four) and bba (length three), so only one string is in L. In the second example, the strings are ababb (length five) and bbbb (length four).

You can think of this way of thinking about distinguishability as a "distinguishability game." … You win the game if you can find a suffix you can tack on to both strings that puts one in L and keeps the other out of L. … There are no restrictions on what kinds of strings you're allowed to append to x and y. The string w you append can be very short (even as short as ε) or very long.

非正则语言: 不存在 DFA、NFA、正则表达式描述它. Myhill-Nerode 定理是证明非正则的主要工具 (见 CS103 18).

distinguishable 可区分: 存在串 w, 使 xw 和 yw 恰有一个属于 L. 把它看成「区分游戏」: 把 x、y 上下写, 在右边找一个共同后缀, 让一个进 L、一个不进. 例: L 是长度恰为 4 的串, aba 和 bb 可区分, 后缀取 a (得 abaa 和 bba) 或 bb (得 ababb 和 bbbb) 都行. 后缀没有任何限制, 可以是 ε, 也可以很长. 找不到任何获胜的后缀, 两串就不可区分.

guide_to_myhill_nerode · Page 2–3

If L is a language over Σ, a distinguishing set for L is a set S⊆Σ⋆ where the following is true: ∀x∈S. ∀y∈S. (x=y→x≡L​y).

… Notice that S is just required to be a subset of Σ* and that there's no requirement that S is a subset of L.

… the language E={anbn∣n∈N} … S={an∣n∈N} is a distinguishing set for E. … suppose we pick two strings am and an out of S, where m ≠ n. … we see two ways to win: ambm vs anbm, or ambn vs anbn. This argument explains why we S is indeed a distinguishing set for E.

… The quantifier ordering here is ∀x. ∀y. ∃w., meaning that we pick x and y arbitrarily first, then get to choose what w is. And, importantly, because of this quantifier ordering, the choice of w can depend on what x and y are.

Theorem: Let L be a language over Σ. If L has an infinite distinguishing set, then L is not regular.

distinguishing set 区分集: S 中任意两个不同的串都对 L 可区分. S 只要是 Σ* 的子集, 不必是 L 的子集; 例如 {an} 是 {anbn} 的区分集, 但 a ∉ E. 证明时: 任取 am=an, 加后缀 bm, 一个属于 E 一个不属于.

量词顺序是 ∀x ∀y ∃w, 后缀 w 可以依赖 x 和 y, 不需要一个对所有对都有效的 w. Myhill-Nerode 定理: L 有无穷区分集 ⟹ L 不是正则的. 要证非正则, 第一反应就是找无穷区分集. 原文 "why we S is" 多了一个 we, "we say that S" 应为 "we saw that S".

寻找区分集
Finding Distinguishing Sets

guide_to_myhill_nerode · Page 3–6

Start Small — … one way to approach finding an infinite distinguishing set is to start off with two distinguishable strings, then find a third string distinguishable from each of those, then a fourth string distinguishable from the three others, etc. until you find a pattern that generalizes.

Let Σ = {a, ≥} and consider this language L: L={am≥an∣m,n∈N∧m≥n}.

… Let's begin with aaaa ≥ aa and aaa ≥ a. … So it looks like we just picked two strings that actually were indistinguishable relative to L. … we accidentally picked two strings where the relative numbers of a's on the sides of the ≥ were the same. … Let's try aaaa ≥ aa and aaaa ≥ aaa … aaaa ≥ aa aa / aaaa ≥ aaa aa … Success!

aaaa ≥ · aaaa ≥ a · aaaa ≥ aa · aaaa ≥ aaa · aaaa ≥ aaaa · aaaa ≥ aaaaa … For example, aaaa ≥ aaaaaa is indistinguishable from aaaa ≥ aaaaa. … If we step away from the aaaa business and instead focus on finding strings with different imbalances, perhaps we'll have some more luck. … S={an≥∣n∈N}.

Proof: Consider the set S={an≥∣n∈N}. … pick any two distinct strings am≥,an≥∈S. … assume, without loss of generality, that m > n. Then we see that am≥am∈L but that an≥am∈/L (since n < m) …

技巧一「从小处开始」: 先找两个可区分的串, 再找第三个、第四个……直到看出能推广的规律. 例子: 左边 a 的个数 ≥ 右边.

  • aaaa ≥ aa 和 aaa ≥ a 不可区分: 两者左右差都是 2, 加同样的后缀后要么都在 L, 要么都不在.
  • 换成差不同的 aaaa ≥ aa 和 aaaa ≥ aaa: 加 aa 后一个差 0 (在 L), 一个差 −1 (不在), 可区分.
  • 扩充到 aaaa ≥ 后接 0 到 5 个 a, 共 6 个串; 再加 6 个 a 就和 5 个不可区分了 (都已超出, 无法挽回), 所以「aaaa 开头」的方向走不到无穷.
  • 真正关键的是左右差 (imbalance). 每个差取最简单的代表: 差 n 的串取 an≥. 于是 S={an≥}.

正式证明: 任取 m > n, 后缀取 am: am≥am∈L, an≥am∈/L. 指南强调这种试错过程很正常, 并不是看定义就能直接想到. 碰巧这里 S ⊆ L, 但一般不必如此. 原文 "or more less at random" 应为 "more or less".

guide_to_myhill_nerode · Page 6–7

What "Must" You Remember? — {w∈Σ⋆∣w has the same number of a’s and b’s}. … How about, say, abba and aaabbb? Are they distinguishable relative to L? Alas, no. … This immediately signals something to us - we're going to have to look for strings that are not in L if we're going to find an infinite distinguishing set.

… A DFA reads the characters of an input string from left to right, then, only at the end, decides whether to accept or reject. Now, a DFA only has finitely many states … Therefore, the DFA has to operate by "summarizing" the string it's seen thus far and just remembering that summary.

Choose each string in the distinguishing set to correspond to different pieces of information that "must" be remembered.

… One simple way to do this is to pick S={an∣n∈N}. The string an has a relative balance of +n … Specifically, pick w=bm. Then we see that amw=ambm∈L because it has m a's and m b's. On the other hand, anw=anbm∈/L because it has n a's but m ≠ n b's. ■

"Hey wait a minute," you might be saying, "isn't that the same distinguishing set that we used for E={anbn∣n∈N}?" Yes. Yes it is. That's not a problem - the same set can serve as a distinguishing set for multiple languages.

技巧二「DFA 必须记住什么」: 语言是 a、b 个数相同的串. L 中的串 (abba、aaabbb) 两两不可区分, 因为它们的相对差都是 0. 所以区分集必须用 L 以外的串.

思路: DFA 只有有限个状态, 却要处理无穷多个串, 所以只能记住已读部分的一个「摘要」(如「含 aa」DFA 的三个状态各对应一种摘要). 识别这个语言的自动机必须记住 a 比 b 多几个, 这个差可以是 0、±1、±2……无穷多种. 为每种「必须记住的信息」选一个代表串, 就得到区分集: {an}, 用后缀 bm 区分. 同一个集合可以是多个语言的区分集. 原文 "distingushing" 是拼写错误.

guide_to_myhill_nerode · Page 7–10

Consider Changing Distinguishing Sets — L={a2n∣n∈N}. … suppose we decide to try using S={an∣n∈N} as a distinguishing set. … The answer is "yes, technically." … Given two strings am and an, where m ≠ n, we'd need to somehow prove there was a number k where exactly one of m and n is a power of two. It's certainly possible to do this (it's a true statement), but this is decidedly nontrivial.

… It looks like every pair of powers of two we look at can be distinguished by appending the shorter of the two strings to both. That might counsel us to pick S={a2n∣n∈N}, or, stated differently, to pick S = L.

Proof: We will show that L is an infinite distinguishing set for itself … pick any distinct strings a2m,a2n∈L and assume without loss of generality that m < n. … a2ma2m=a2m+2m=a2⋅2m=a2m+1, which means that a2ma2m∈L. … there exists a natural number k such that n = m + k + 1. We thus see that 2n+2m=2m+k+1+2m=2m(2k+1+1)=2m(2⋅2k+1). We note that 2⋅2k+1 is odd. Moreover, … 2⋅2k+1≥3. Therefore, 2n+2m has an odd divisor greater than or equal to three, which means that 2n+2m is not a power of two. ■

技巧三「考虑换一个区分集」: 长度为 2 的幂的串. 用 {an} 理论上可行, 但要对任意 m ≠ n 找出 k, 使 m + k 和 n + k 恰有一个是 2 的幂, 证明很麻烦 (例如 a⁶ 和 a¹⁴: 补 2 个 a 会让两者都变成 2 的幂 8 和 16, 要补 10 个或 18 个才行).

改用 L 自身作区分集: 两个 2 的幂长度的串, 都补上较短的那个. 较短的变成 2m+1, 是 2 的幂; 较长的变成 2m(2k+1+1), 有大于 1 的奇因子, 不是 2 的幂. 换成形状更受限的串, 能省掉大量分情况讨论. 区分集可以就是语言本身.

原文错误: "there was a number k where exactly one of m and n is a power of two" 应为 "exactly one of m + k and n + k is a power of two". 要找的是后缀 ak, 判断的是补完之后的长度; m、n 本身是否为 2 的幂与 k 无关. 另有笔误: "distinguishign" (distinguishing)、"amely" (namely).

Exercises

guide_to_myhill_nerode · Page 10
  1. Let Σ = {a, b} and let L be the following language over Σ: L={w∈Σ⋆∣∣w∣ is odd and the middle character of w is a}. Prove that L is not regular.
  2. Let Σ = {a, b} and consider the finite language L = {ε, a}. Draw the smallest possible DFA for L. … Then, prove that every DFA for L has at least as many states as your DFA. To do so, use the following theorem …: if S is a distinguishing set for L containing finitely many strings, then any DFA for L must have at least |S| states.
  3. Let Σ be an arbitrary alphabet and let L be an arbitrary language where L ≠ Σ* and L ≠ ∅. Prove that L has a distinguishing set of cardinality two.
  4. … Let L ⊆ E be a language where |L| is infinite. Prove that L is not regular.
  5. Let Σ = {a}. Prove that S={an∣n∈N} is a distinguishing set for L={an2∣n∈N}.

答案要点:

  1. S={bn}. 对 m < n, 后缀取 abm: bmabm 长度奇数且中间是 a, 在 L 中; bnabm 若长度为偶数则不在 L, 若为奇数, 中间位置落在前面的 bn 段 (因为 n > m), 中间字符是 b, 也不在 L.
  2. 最小 DFA 3 个状态: 起始 (接受, 对应 ε)、读了 a (接受)、陷阱 (其余). 区分集 {ε, a, b}: ε 与 a 用后缀 a 区分 (a ∈ L, aa ∉ L); ε 与 b、a 与 b 用后缀 ε 区分. 所以任何 DFA 至少 3 个状态.
  3. L 非空, 取 x ∈ L; L 不是全体, 取 y ∉ L. 后缀 ε 就区分了它们, {x, y} 是大小为 2 的区分集.
  4. 令 S = { aⁿ | aⁿbⁿ ∈ L }, L 无穷所以 S 无穷. 对 m ≠ n, 后缀 bm: ambm∈L, 而 anbm∈/E⊇L.
  5. 对 m < n, 取足够大的 j 使 2j + 1 > n − m 且 j² ≥ m, 后缀取 aj2−m: 前者长度 j² 是平方数; 后者长度 j² + (n − m) 严格介于 j² 和 (j + 1)² 之间, 不是平方数.

上下文无关文法指南
Guide to CFGs

guide_to_cfgs · Page 1

Context-free grammars are a powerful and flexible tool for specifying languages, but they can take some time to get used to … This handout covers three major techniques useful in the design of context-free grammars:

  • Find a build order. CFGs construct strings in a different order than what you might naturally expect.
  • Think inductively and recursively. Fundamentally, CFGs work by identifying some recursive structure of the strings in a language.
  • Store information in nonterminals. Using different nonterminals to represent different parts of a string, or different fundamental classes of strings, makes it possible to build CFGs for elaborate structures like spoken and programming languages.

设计 CFG 的三种技巧: 找到构造顺序 (CFG 生成串的顺序和直觉不同); 归纳地、递归地思考 (找出串的递归结构); 用非终结符存储信息 (不同的非终结符代表串的不同部分或不同类别). 对应 CS103 19.

找到构造顺序
Find a Build Order

guide_to_cfgs · Page 1–2

… let's take this sample CFG for the language {anbn∣n∈N}: S → aSb | ε. … S ⇒ aSb ⇒ aaSbb ⇒ aaaSbbb ⇒ aaaaSbbbb ⇒ aaaabbbb

… each a is placed down along with one matching b symbol. … Intuitively, you might think that they'd pair off this way: … the first a would pair with the first b, the second a with the second b, etc. However, that's not actually what happens here. … they're matched from the outside in (or inside out, same thing).

☞ CFGs match items from the outside in. ☜

L = { w ∈ {a, b}* | w's length is a multiple of three, and the first third of its characters are a's }

aa|aaaa · a|bb · aa|abbb · aa|baba · aaa|bbbbbb … there's twice as many characters after the line as there are before the line. … the first character will pair with the last two characters, and the second character will pair with the two characters before those, etc.

aⁿbⁿ 的文法 S → aSb | ε 每次在两端各放一个字符, 所以配对方式是由外向内: 第一个 a 配最后一个 b, 第二个 a 配倒数第二个 b, 而不是直觉上的「第一个配第一个」. 记住: CFG 从外向内匹配.

例子: 长度是 3 的倍数、前三分之一全是 a 的串. 先写正反例, 再在前三分之一处画竖线, 发现竖线后面的字符数是前面的两倍, 于是让前面每个字符配后面两个字符, 而且按由外向内配: 第一个字符配最后两个.

guide_to_cfgs · Page 2–3

S → aSbb // still a work in progress … First, we have no way to stop! … Second, we're building a string where the back two-thirds of the string are always b's …

S → aSbb | ε // still a work in progress … we have a perfectly correct grammar for the language {anb2n∣n∈N}. … But it's still work pausing here to appreciate how we got here!

… we can't just write S → aSΣΣ and call it a day. In CFG Land, Σ just means “the character Σ” and isn't a catch-all for “any one character.” … S → aSaa | aSab | aSba | aSbb | ε … However, I'm not a huge fan of this strategy. … (with {a, b, c}) S → aSaa | aSab | aSac | aSba | aSbb | aSbc | aSca | aScb | aScc | ε

… Imagine you were asked to write a CFG just for the language of all length-one strings over the alphabet {a, b, c}. … T → a | b | c … the nonterminal T we built here means “any one character,” so T T would mean “any two characters.”

S → aSTT | ε
T → a | b | c

逐步修正: S → aSbb 停不下来, 而且后面只能是 b; 加上 S → ε 后得到 anb2n 的正确文法, 但还不是目标语言. 后两个字符可以任意: CFG 里 Σ 只是一个普通字符, 不能表示「任意字符」; 把 aa、ab、ba、bb 四种组合全列出来能行, 但字母表一大就爆炸 ({a, b, c} 要 9 条). 更好的办法: 用非终结符 T → a | b | c 表示「任意一个字符」, TT 就是任意两个字符. 最终 S → aSTT | ε.

要点: 表达「任意一个字符」时, 定义一个专门的非终结符, 让文法的写法和意图一致. 原文 "still work pausing" 应为 "worth pausing", "we've build up" 应为 "built".

归纳地、递归地思考
Think Inductively and Recursively

guide_to_cfgs · Page 3–5

… We can think of S → ε as being a base case … Think of the S in “aSb” as a placeholder for “some string in the language {aⁿbⁿ | n ∈ ℕ}.” This rule then says “given a string in the language, you can form another string in the language by taking that string, putting an a on the front, and putting a b on the back.” … the rule S → aSb means “to see if your string is in the language, if it starts with a and ends with b, then you can cross off the a and b at the beginning and end and recursively check whether what you have is still in the language.”

L = { w ∈ {a, b}* | w's length is a multiple of three, and the first third of the characters in w contains at least one a }

bbabb|aabaaabbab → babb|aabaaabb → abb|aabaaa → bb|aaba … Now we're left with a string that isn't in the language. … When we crossed off a b those times, we knew that what we were left with would still have to have an a somewhere in the front … But when we crossed off an a from the front, what we're left with doesn't have to have any more a's at the front.

T → UUUT | ε
U → a | b

S → bSUU | aTUU
T → UUUT | ε
U → a | b

产生式的两种读法: 归纳地看, S → ε 是基础情形, S → aSb 是「已有一个属于语言的串, 两端加 a 和 b 得到新串」; 递归地看, 是「判断一个串时, 若首 a 尾 b, 划掉两端再递归判断」.

新例子: 前三分之一至少有一个 a (把上一例的全称改成存在). 从一个属于 L 的串开始, 反复划掉首字符和末尾两个字符: 划掉的是 b 时, 剩下的串仍在 L 中 (那个 a 还在前面); 划掉的是 a 时, 剩下的串只需长度是 3 的倍数, 没有别的要求 (例子里第三次划掉 a 后得到 bb|aaba, 不在 L 中, 但长度仍是 3 的倍数). 于是需要两类串: S (属于 L) 和 T (长度是 3 的倍数). T → UUUT | ε 每次生成三个任意字符. 合起来: S → bSUU | aTUU.

原文 "crossed of a b" 应为 "crossed off".

用非终结符存储信息
Store Information in Nonterminals

guide_to_cfgs · Page 5–7

… We can therefore think of a derivation starting with S as consisting of “apply the recursive rule SbSUU until you're satisfied with the result, then apply the production S → aTUU to switch from S to T.” … S ⇒ bSUU (“let's do it again!”) ⇒ bbSUUUU (“yay! more recursion!”) ⇒ bbaTUUUUUU (“okay, ready to move on now.”) At this point, we're free to whatever T-ish sorts of things we want to do.

… We can think of S and T not, as we did before, as standing for classes of strings, but rather as functioning more like the states of a DFA or NFA.

{ w ∈ {a, b}* | w's length is a multiple of three, and the first third of w has at least three a's }

aaa|aaaaaa · aaa|bbbbbb · ababa|bababababa · baaa|baaabaaa · abaa|bbbbbbbb · aaab|bbbbbbbb

S → bSWW | aTWW
T → bTWW | aUWW
U → bUWW | aVWW
V → WWWV | ε
W → a | b

Play around with this one – can you tell which nonterminals correspond to which counts?

另一种看法: S 和 T 不是两类串, 而像自动机的状态. 处在 S 时是「第一阶段」, 在前面放 b、在后面放两个任意字符; 用 S → aTUU 切换到 T 后是「第二阶段」, 在中间填长度为 3 的倍数的任意串.

推广到「前三分之一至少三个 a」: 让非终结符记录「还需要几个 a」. S 还需 3 个, T 还需 2 个, U 还需 1 个, V 不再需要 (只要求长度是 3 的倍数). 前面放 b 时停在原状态, 放 a 时进入下一个状态. 这就回答了原文最后的问题. 我们用 Python 生成了这个文法长度 ≤ 9 的所有串, 与语言定义完全一致.

原文笔误: "apply the recursive rule SbSUU" 漏了箭头, 应为 S → bSUU; "we're free to whatever" 漏了 do.

guide_to_cfgs · Page 7

Some Exercises

  1. Let Σ = {a, b} and let L={anbm∣m,n∈N and n≤m≤5n}. Write a CFG for L.
  2. Let Σ = {a, b, c} and let L={ambncp∣m,n,p∈N and m=n or m=p}. Write a CFG for L.
  3. Let Σ = {a, b} and let L={anbm∣m,n∈N and m=n}. Write a CFG for L.
  4. Let Σ = {a, b} and let L = { w ∈ Σ* | w's length is a multiple of three and the first third of w contains an odd number of a's }. Write a CFG for L.

参考答案 (都用 Python 生成短串, 与语言定义逐一比对过):

  1. S → aSb | aSbb | aSbbb | aSbbbb | aSbbbbb | ε. 每放一个 a 配 1 到 5 个 b.
  2. S → XC | Y, X → aXb | ε, C → cC | ε, Y → aYc | B, B → bB | ε. 两种情况分开写再并起来: m = n 时 a 与 b 配对, c 任意; m = p 时 a 与 c 由外向内配对, 中间的 b 任意.
  3. S → aSb | A | B, A → aA | a, B → bB | b. 先由外向内配对, 最后中间剩下至少一个多余的 a 或至少一个多余的 b.
  4. S → bSUU | aTUU, T → bTUU | aSUU | ε, U → a | b. S 表示「前面还需要奇数个 a」, T 表示「还需要偶数个 a」, 每放一个 a 就在两者之间切换, 只有 T 可以结束.

自指指南与熔岩图指南
Guide to Self-Reference · Guide to the Lava Diagram

guide_to_self_reference · guide_to_the_lava_diagram · Page 1

Guide to Self-Reference — This animated guide explains how to prove languages are undecidable using self-reference. Guide to Self-Reference

Guide to the Lava Diagram — This animated guide explains how to categorize languages as regular, decidable, recognizable, or unrecognizable. Guide to the Lava Diagram

两份动画指南的入口: 一份讲如何用自指证明语言不可判定 (见 CS103 22、23), 一份讲如何把语言归类为正则、可判定、可识别或不可识别 (见 CS103 25).

自指证明的固定套路 (课上的版本): 假设语言 L 可判定 (或可识别), 写一个程序 trickster, 它调用自己的源代码和 L 的判定器, 先问「我会不会做某事」, 然后反着做. 无论判定器回答什么都会矛盾, 所以判定器不存在.

熔岩图归类的思路: 先问是否正则 (能否写出 DFA / 正则表达式, 或用 Myhill-Nerode 证明不能); 不是正则就问能否写出总会停机的判定器 (在 R 中); 不能就问能否写出验证器或识别器 (在 RE 中); 补语言在 RE 中则属于 co-RE. 既不在 RE 也不在 co-RE 的语言 (如 {⟨M⟩∣L(M)=Σ⋆}) 在最外层.

LaTeX 指南
Guide to LaTeX

guide_to_latex · Page 1

In CS103, we require you to type your problem sets. While you can use pretty much any system you'd like for this (Microsoft Word, LibreOffice, Google Docs, etc.), we encourage you to use LaTeX. LaTeX is a mathematical typesetting system. It's widely used in academia for typesetting papers, posters, and books.

… We recommend the lovely online tool Overleaf. … click the "New Project" button. … you'll be taken to a screen with two panes. On the right you'll see a PDF containing some sample text. On the right you'll see the raw LaTeX source that generated that document.

\documentclass{article}
\usepackage[utf8]{inputenc}
\title{Test Project}
\author{htiek}
\date{April 2024}
\begin{document}
\maketitle
\section{Introduction}
\end{document}
Hello, world! Watch me do math: $(x + 1)^2 = x^2 + 2x + 1$.
\LaTeX can do other things too. Here's a fraction: $\frac{137}{42}$.

… Plain text just displays as-is. When you surround text with the $ character, it somehow starts thinking that you're doing Mathy Things. Special commands start with the \ character, and curly braces are used for arguments or to group things together.

CS103 要求作业打字提交, 推荐用 LaTeX 排版 (学术界写论文、海报、书的标准工具, 基础几个小时就能学会). 推荐在线编辑器 Overleaf: 新建项目后, 一边是源码, 一边是编译出的 PDF. 在 \section{Introduction} 下面写文字和 $…$ 里的公式, 点 recompile 就能看到上标、分数等排版效果.

三条基本规则: 普通文字原样显示; 用 $ 包起来的部分进入数学模式; 命令以 \ 开头, 花括号用来传参数或分组.

原文笔误: "On the right you'll see a PDF … On the right you'll see the raw LaTeX source" 两处都写成 right, 其中一处应为 left (Overleaf 默认左边是源码、右边是 PDF). 另有 "You should see see" 多一个 see, "superscrips" 应为 superscripts, "intepreted" 应为 interpreted.

guide_to_latex · Page 1–2

Text Mode and Math Mode — LaTeX has two modes: text mode, where characters are written out as text, and math mode, which is used for equations. … Use the $ character to surround what you want to include in math mode.

  • Powers and exponents can be done using the ^ operator. For example, $x^2 + 5$ renders as x2+5.
  • Subscripts can be done using the _ operator. For example, $F_2 = F_0 + F_1$ renders as F2​=F0​+F1​.

… by default, only a single character is picked up by the ^ or _ operators. For example, if we write $x^42 = a_137$, we get x42=a1​37, which doesn't match the intuitive mathematical meaning. … x^{42} = a_{137} will render as x42=a137​ … $x^{y^{z_2}}$ renders as xyz2​.

… you can surround text with two dollar signs ($$) to have that text intepreted as math, but then displayed on its own line and centered.

The quadratic formula says that the solutions to $ax^2 + bx + c = 0$ are
given by $$\frac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a},$$ a formula that is commonly
memorized in early algebra courses.

… The command \pm is the "plus or minus" symbol. To display a fraction, we use the syntax \frac{numerator}{denominator}. And to do a square root, we write \sqrt{expression}.

LaTeX 有文本模式和数学模式两种. 数学模式里: ^ 上标, _ 下标; 它们默认只管一个字符, 所以 x^42 会显示成 x² 后面跟一个 4, 多个字符要用花括号: x^{42}. 上下标可以嵌套 (x^{y^{z_2}}). 单个 $ 是行内公式, $$ 是单独成行居中的公式. 常用命令: \pm (±)、\frac{分子}{分母}、\sqrt{表达式}.

In case you're wondering what \mathbb means, it's "math blackboard bold," the fancy name for those sorts of symbols.

Writing out actual sets is a bit trickier. Remember that LaTeX treats curly braces as something that groups mathematical expressions together. As a result, if you write {1, 2, 3}, it'll display as 1, 2, 3. To explicitly write out those braces, write it out like this: \{1, 2, 3\} … it's really easy to forget to do this, and leaving off braces can change the mathematical meaning of what you write!

Other Symbols — … One option would be to check our LaTeX templates … Another option would be to use the remarkable website Detexify. Draw whatever symbol you're looking for, and it will suggest possible options for what you want.

集合相关的常用命令见表: 并、交、差、对称差、属于、不属于、子集、非子集、基数、幂集 (\wp 是魏尔斯特拉斯 p 的花体)、空集、黑板粗体的 ℕ ℤ ℝ (\mathbb 即 math blackboard bold)、ℵ0​.

易错: 花括号在 LaTeX 里是分组符号, 直接写 {1, 2, 3} 不会显示括号, 要写成 \{1, 2, 3\}, 否则集合的意思就丢了. 找不到符号时可以查课程模板, 或在 Detexify 网站上手画符号让它识别.

两点补充: 集合差在标准 LaTeX 中更规范的写法是 \setminus; \backslash 是普通的反斜杠字符, 两边间距不同 (课程网页用 MathJax 渲染, 两者看起来差不多). 不属于可以直接写 \notin, 比 \not\in 的斜线位置更好看.
